As you walk with me through its enchanting narrow alleys, sun-drenched squares, and timeless architecture, you will discover the soul of a city that has preserved its medieval essence while embracing the charm of the modern world. Let us embark on a journey through centuries of history, culture, and beauty. Porto Maurizio’s roots delve deep into antiquity, with early settlements dating back to Roman times. Due to its favorable coastal position, the settlement thrived as a hub for maritime trade and communication across the Mediterranean. The name "Porto Maurizio" likely derives from the patron saint, Saint Maurice, reflecting the strong religious influence that has shaped the town’s identity over the centuries. During the Middle Ages, Porto Maurizio became a vital political and religious center. Perched dramatically on a hill overlooking the shimmering Ligurian Sea, the old town known as Parasio emerged as the town's fortified core. With its stone-paved alleys known as "caruggi," colorful pastel houses, and panoramic views, Parasio is a true masterpiece of medieval urban planning. Walk with me through these winding alleys where every turn reveals new wonders—tiny chapels, rustic courtyards, and ornate doorways that whisper stories from ages past. One cannot speak of Porto Maurizio without mentioning its most iconic landmark—the Basilica of San Maurizio. Built between 1781 and 1832, it is the largest church in Liguria and a stunning example of neoclassical architecture. Its massive white façade stands proudly above the town, while its richly adorned interior tells the story of the town’s religious devotion and artistic excellence. The basilica represents a time when Porto Maurizio was a beacon of wealth, culture, and spiritual importance. The spiritual significance of Porto Maurizio is further highlighted by the many churches and religious institutions found throughout the town. The Oratory of San Pietro and the Church of Santa Chiara are notable examples, each showcasing exquisite religious art, ancient relics, and centuries of devotion. Religious processions, once common in Porto Maurizio’s narrow streets, still take place today, offering a glimpse into the town’s vibrant traditions. Economically, Porto Maurizio flourished from the 12th to the 16th centuries, fueled by maritime trade, agriculture, and the production of olive oil—a staple of Ligurian life. The fertile hills surrounding the town have long been adorned with olive groves, producing some of Italy’s finest olive oils. The ancient terraced landscapes, crafted with dry-stone walls, reflect the intimate relationship between the people and their land. Even today, traditional olive oil production remains a proud part of the town’s economy and culture. Throughout its history, Porto Maurizio faced numerous challenges, from pirate raids to conflicts with the powerful maritime republic of Genoa. Despite these adversities, the town managed to preserve its independence and identity until it was incorporated into Genoese control in the 16th century. In 1923, Porto Maurizio merged with neighboring Oneglia and other communities to form the city of Imperia. However, the distinct character and spirit of Porto Maurizio remain palpable and vibrant. The modern visitor to Porto Maurizio is greeted by an intoxicating blend of history and natural beauty. Strolling along the ancient paths, one encounters breathtaking views of the Ligurian coastline, quaint artisan shops, and cafes nestled in centuries-old buildings. The air is filled with the scent of sea breeze and blooming flowers, while the soft hum of life in the piazzas evokes a timeless sense of peace and community. The town’s harbor area provides a lively contrast to the serene old town. Here, colorful fishing boats bob gently in the crystal-clear waters, and bustling seafood markets offer the freshest catches of the day. Along the waterfront, cozy trattorias serve delicious Ligurian cuisine, from freshly made pesto to delicate seafood pastas. Dining by the sea as the sun sets behind the hills is an experience that captures the very essence of Porto Maurizio’s charm. Porto Maurizio also celebrates its maritime heritage through events like the Vele d'Epoca di Imperia, a prestigious regatta featuring historic sailing vessels from around the world. This event transforms the harbor into a spectacular showcase of nautical history and craftsmanship, attracting visitors, historians, and sailing enthusiasts alike. The architectural wealth of Porto Maurizio is truly astounding. Beyond the grand basilica, the town boasts a wide array of historic buildings, elegant palaces, and artistic treasures. The medieval layout of Parasio, with its maze of alleys and arches, is a testament to the ingenuity and resilience of its medieval builders. Many of the old palaces now house museums, galleries, and cultural centers, preserving the town’s rich artistic heritage for future generations. Art lovers will appreciate the delicate frescoes, intricate stone carvings, and beautiful mosaics that adorn the town’s churches and public spaces. Each work of art serves as a bridge to the past, connecting the modern traveler with the artisans, architects, and visionaries who shaped Porto Maurizio’s cultural landscape. The natural surroundings of Porto Maurizio are equally captivating. The Ligurian coastline offers spectacular hiking trails that wind along cliffs and through ancient olive groves, providing panoramic views of the Mediterranean. title: ⚡ ¿Puede un Apagón Acabar con Todo?: La Fragilidad de Nuestra Civilización
text: Imagine walking through your city on any given morning. The sun rises, cars are driving, cell phones are vibrating in our pockets... and suddenly, in just five seconds, 60% of the entire country's electricity is gone. The street lights went out. Traffic lights become just black boxes. The shops are dark. Bars cannot serve coffee. Phones stop working. Wi-Fi becomes a memory. And you're there in the middle of it all wondering: What the hell is going on? It's not a science fiction scene. It's not the beginning of The Walking Dead, nor is it a dystopia ripped from Mark Ellsberg's Blackout. This is what happened and we saw it with our own eyes. On Monday, April 28, 2025, Spain and Portugal experienced the largest power outage in their history. The power outage also left Andorra and part of southern France without electricity, compounding the impact of the blackout. A massive blackout that lasted for hours paralyzed cities, infrastructure, and communications... and made us look back to a time when we still lived without electricity. You might wonder: How can a modern country, full of satellites, servers, switchboards, and sensors, in the 21st century, fall into total darkness from one second to the next? Well, today, we're going to shine a light—literally and figuratively—on this everyday yet mysterious phenomenon: electricity. We'll discover what really happened during the Great Blackout, and above all, why our world depends so much on something as invisible as it is fragile. Are you ready? I am GG Prigo, this is the science of sciences, here we always see that the known is limited and the unknown is infinite. Want to know more? Well... let's explore! Introduction Yes, what comes out of our light bulbs is not a modern luxury. It is the beating heart of our civilization. To begin to understand this, we need to look at what exactly happened. At 12:32 p.m., an unusual event rocked the Iberian electricity grid: 15 gigawatts of power suddenly disappeared—more than half of the country's total consumption at the time. Yes, suddenly. As if someone had uprooted a fundamental part of the system. To give you an idea, this is roughly equivalent to cutting off twice Spain's operational nuclear capacity immediately. Real anger. It was like being in the middle of a game of Jenga and someone was pulling out the tile that was keeping the entire tower upright. The system has crashed, the grid has been disconnected from Europe, and we have gone into power survival mode. This is where things get more interesting. Because we're so used to flipping a switch and seeing the light come on... that we forget to ask the key question: What is electricity, really? No, they are not magic lines. Electricity is the orderly movement of electrons. Millions and millions of them, flowing through cables, like an invisible river of tiny particles that give life to our cities, our homes, our hospitals, our satellites... and to you. Imagine it this way: if water flows in a river, electrons flow in wires. It is not that there is a “thing” that travels as if it were a train. no! It's the electrons of the atoms themselves that are moving collectively, a kind of microscopic collapse. Here comes the really amazing thing: electricity is not stored on a large scale. They are generated in real time. Every time you turn on a light bulb, there is a power station generating that energy at that specific moment. text: The participants were asked to reflect on their experiences in the contract relationship, sharing how it felt and how it shaped their connection. Ha-neul shared, "It felt so real, like we weren’t in contract relationship. It was as if we were truly dating. Woo-jae admitted, "When the contract ended, it felt like a real breakup. It was bittersweet, but I think it gave us a chance to explore our true feelings." Jimin shared, "I didn’t know what the future held, but I wanted to hold onto our moments together. text: Tham gently told me, "You are very lucky, sir. You only have bruises and a slight dislocation. If you had broken a bone, it would have been very difficult for both you and your children and grandchildren." Hearing what the doctor said, I was lost in thought, right, if something worse happened to me , who would take care of me? My children are all far away, who will be the one to come and pick me up? I just wanted to satisfy my hobby of traveling and forgot that old age is not like youth anymore. Even a small fall can have immeasurable consequences, even leaving you bedridden for the rest of your life. Since that accident, I no longer have the desire or desire to travel far away. I realized that it is not necessary to travel a lot to enjoy life. How many simple joys are there just around the corner? It's just that I've been chasing after distant things without realizing it. I started spending more time walking around my neighborhood, chatting with friendly neighbors, and tending to my small vegetable garden behind my house. My old friends and I joined a health club. Every morning we go to the park together to do light, healthy exercises. I still visit my hometown but don't go too far anymore, just to visit my children and grandchildren during the day and then return home immediately. I also learned to listen to the signals from my body. Before I got married subjectively thinking that I was still very healthy. But in fact, the health of the elderly is as fragile as a flickering lamp in the wind. Just a strong wind or a small collision can cause the lamp to go out at any time. I no longer try to do things beyond my body's endurance . If I have to go somewhere a little further, I always arrange to have my children or relatives go with me for peace of mind. I absolutely do not take long-distance buses alone anymore, and do not go to places that are risky or dangerous anymore. Now, my days pass by gently and peacefully. I no longer worry or fret about long trips. Because I joke that true happiness is not about how far you have gone but about whether you feel safe and satisfied right where you are. Dear friends , when we are young, we have enough health and enthusiasm to travel everywhere and discover the myriad new things of the world. But when old age knocks on the door, the most important thing is no longer where to go but how to maintain health and maintain peace for yourself. The ancients said, "The one who knows when to stop is the wise one." If we stubbornly want to go far, want to do things beyond our ability and health, in the end we can only bring bad things upon ourselves, even into ourselves. For that reason, be brave enough to close the door called going away. If you really want to go somewhere for a change of scenery, prioritize choosing places that are close, familiar and easy to get to. In case you have to go far, try to arrange to have a relative or friend go with you. Never go out alone. Most importantly, if you feel unwell or tired, don't force yourself. Know when to stop and rest. Now I feel my life has become much lighter and more relaxed. I have no desire to go far anymore. But strangely, I feel happier , more peaceful. Because I know I'm living a peaceful life. No more worries or potential dangers. You see, old age is not the time to chase after luxurious trips but the time to cherish and enjoy the simple joys right before your eyes. If you feel this story brings meaning and valuable lessons, please don't forget to click the like button, share this story with more people and subscribe to the channel to spread meaningful lessons together, helping each person's old age to be more peaceful and happy. title: ONE PIECE 🏴‍☠️ e As Mensagens ANARQUISTAS de Eiichiro Oda
text: One Piece is an incredible work, but I'm not going to lie: it's difficult to start watching. With more than a thousand episodes, the idea of ​​diving into this universe can scare anyone. But the truth is, after watching the first 300 episodes, you finally understand why Eiichiro Oda is a genius. Some scenes and moments are so impactful that they make each episode worth watching. My Experience with One Piece. I've never been a big fan of piracy stories and, honestly, I've always been too lazy to download One Piece to watch. But after it came on Netflix, I decided to give it a chance. And that's when I realized: people were right. Eiichiro Oda truly is a genius. The construction of the world, the characters, the emotions... all of this made me fall in love with the work. Iconic Moments. One Piece has some scenes that make it worth watching 500, 600 episodes just to feel the emotion for the first time. An example of this is the scene where Luffy puts the hat on Nami, a moment of pure trust and friendship. Another moment that stood out to me was when Luffy orders the World Government flag to be burned. It was at that moment that I realized that Oda was teaching something much bigger: the government is the real enemy. This made me become a fan of him and One Piece. But without a doubt, the most iconic scene of all is when Luffy punches a Tenryuubito. And if you don't know what a Tenryuubito is, they are members of the "world nobility", an arrogant elite who live above everyone else, treating ordinary people like trash. They dress ridiculously, with bubble helmets so they don't breathe the same air as normal people. This is very reminiscent of our politicians: distant from reality, living in bubbles of privilege and believing that they are above the laws. When Luffy lands that punch, it's like the cry of millions of people who suffer from injustice every day. It's one of the most satisfying moments in the entire work. It's a good thing that One Piece is a long work, because to understand these deep messages, you need to watch many episodes and get involved with the world created by Oda. If it were a short and direct series , with such open criticism, there would certainly be countries where the government would try to ban it from being shown. But as everything is diluted over a thousand episodes, it ends up going unnoticed by those who aren't paying attention. Eiichiro Oda's Anarchist Message. Throughout the entire work, Oda makes it clear that the greatest evil in the world is oppression coming from rulers. The World Government manipulates history, hides secrets and exploits the weakest. This becomes even more evident when we see the Tenryuubito, a rotten elite who think they are superior to everyone. And nothing symbolizes the revolt against this system more than the iconic scene of Luffy punching a Tenryuubito without hesitation. This scene is the personification of the fight against tyranny. Conclusion. One Piece is much more than a story about pirates searching for treasure. It is a powerful social commentary on freedom, oppression and resistance. Oda uses his narrative to teach us that the true enemy has always been the system that limits and controls us. If you haven't watched One Piece yet, give it a chance. It may take a while for you to get involved, but once you understand the message behind the work, you will realize why this story is one of the greatest of all time. title: Execution of Hungarian prime minister who killed 330,000 men, women & children at Auschwitz
text: March 1944, Hungary. As the tide of the Second World War shifts decisively against Nazi Germany, Hungarian Regent Miklós Horthy finds himself under growing pressure, both domestically and from Berlin, to determine where Hungary truly stands. Behind the scenes, the Hungarian Prime Minister Miklós Kállay, increasingly convinced that Germany’s defeat is inevitable, has been discreetly reaching out to the Western Allies in hopes of securing a separate peace and avoiding Soviet occupation. These secret efforts, however, do not go unnoticed by the Germans. On 19 March 1944, under the codename Operation Margarethe, German troops enter Hungary and swiftly occupy the country without firing a single shot. In the days that follow, Horthy is confronted with a stark ultimatum from Hitler: either appoint a pro-German prime minister who will fully cooperate with the Nazi leadership or accept total occupation, a move that would effectively strip Hungary of all remaining sovereignty. Faced with this dilemma, and fearing the fate that had already befallen countries like Poland and France, Horthy reluctantly agrees to replace Kállay. While Germans strongly recommend Béla Imrédy, a former prime minister known for his fanatical pro-German stance and his implementation of antisemitic policies, Horthy—deeply uneasy about Imrédy’s extremism—instead proposes a seemingly more moderate figure. He will choose a man who will help Germans to kill hundreds of thousands of Hungarian citizens. His name is Döme Sztójay. Döme Sztójay was born as Dimitrije Stojaković on 5 January 1883 in the city of Versec, then part of Austria-Hungary. He came from a Serbian family and pursued a military career, studying at the cadet school in Pécs and later at the Military Academy in Vienna. During the First World War, which started on 28 July 1914, Sztójay served in the Austro-Hungarian Army and led the Balkan group of the military intelligence service. Hungary had been on the losing side of World War I, which ended on 11 November 1918. On 4 June 1920 Hungary signed the Treaty of Trianon which reduced the country’s territory by 72%. In addition, Hungary lost its sea access, half of its 10 biggest cities and all of its precious metal mines. The post-1920 Hungary had a population of 7.6 million, 36% compared to the pre-war kingdom's population of 20.9 million, and 3,425,000 ethnic Hungarians found themselves separated from their motherland. In June 1919, Admiral Miklós Horthy, who had been an officer in the Austro-Hungarian navy, came to power as the head of a conservative-nationalist coalition. Horthy presided for the next 24 years over an authoritarian, almost feudal system of aristocratic rule, which nevertheless had a functioning parliament and permitted political opposition. After Horthy became Regent of Hungary, Sztójay was promoted to general and served as a military attaché in Berlin from 1927 to 1933. He Magyarized his name to Sztójay in 1927, and from 1933 to 1935, he served in the Ministry of Defence. In 1935, he became Hungary’s ambassador to Nazi Germany — a position he held for the next nine years. As ambassador, Sztójay formed strong ties with the Third Reich and often voiced support for German policies to his superiors in Hungary. In the late 1930s, as Germany began redrawing national boundaries across Europe, Hungary — with support from Germany and Italy — was able to reclaim lost territory. Before the Second World War began on 1 September 1939, this included southern Slovakia, annexed from Czechoslovakia in 1938, and Subcarpathian Rus, acquired from the dismembered Czechoslovak state in 1939. After the war started, the regained territory included northern Transylvania from Romania in 1940 and the Bačka region from dismembered Yugoslavia, which was attacked in April 1941. In November 1940, Hungary joined the Axis alliance which was a military coalition that initiated World War II and fought against the Allies. In June 1941 Hungarian troops participated alongside German troops in the invasion of the Soviet Union. Hungary fell increasingly under the influence of Germany and many Hungarian politicians called for more radical steps to be taken in solving the so called Jewish Question. According to a 1941 census, Hungary, including the recently annexed territories, had a Jewish population of 825,000, less than 6 percent of the total population. The Hungarian racial laws were modelled on Germany's Nuremberg Laws. These defined "Jews" in so-called racial terms, forbade intermarriage between Jews and non-Jews, and excluded Jews from full participation in various professions. The laws also barred employment of Jews in the civil service and restricted their opportunities in economic life. It was in the summer of 1941 when Hungarian authorities deported some 20,000 Jews, most of whom resided in Subcarpathian Rus and none of whom had been able to obtain Hungarian citizenship. These Jews were deported to the city of Kamenets-Podolski in German-occupied Ukraine, where they were shot by detachments of Einsatzgruppe, which were Nazi mobile death squads. In January 1942, Hungarian military units murdered 3,000 Jews and Serbs in Novi Sad, the major city in the part of Yugoslavia annexed by Hungary. However, in 1942 when the German government began to pressure the Hungarians to deliver Jews who were Hungarian citizens into German custody, Horthy's prime minister, Miklós Kállay, despite significant pressure from the domestic radical right, refused to deport the Hungarian Jews. After the German defeat at Stalingrad in February 1943, Hungarian Admiral Miklós Horthy and Prime Minister Miklós Kállay recognized that Germany would likely lose the war. With Horthy's tacit approval, Kállay tried to negotiate a separate armistice for Hungary with the Western Allies. After the German defeat at Stalingrad in February 1943, Hungarian Admiral Miklós Horthy and Prime Minister Miklós Kállay recognized that Germany would likely lose the war. With Horthy's tacit approval, Kállay tried to negotiate a separate armistice for Hungary with the Western Allies. To prevent these efforts, Adolf Hitler ordered Operation Margarethe—the German occupation of Hungary and on 19 March 1944, German troops entered the country without resistance. By this time, about 63,000 Jews living in Hungary died or were killed. During the German occupation, Horthy was permitted to remain as Regent but Kallay was dismissed. In his place, the Germans installed Döme Sztójay as Prime Minister who immediately aligned Hungarian policy with Nazi interests. Sztójay quickly legalized Ferenc Szálasi’s Arrow Cross Party — a radically antisemitic, Nazi-inspired fascist movement that had previously been banned under Horthy’s leadership. He committed Hungary fully to the Nazi war effort, increasing Hungarian troop deployments on the Eastern Front and cracking down on political opposition. Labor unions were dissolved, left-wing politicians were jailed, and civil liberties were severely restricted. Most notably, Sztójay oversaw dramatic escalation in the persecution of Hungarian Jews. On 31 March 1944, a decree required all Jews over the age of six to wear a yellow six-pointed star on their clothing, starting 5 April. In April 1944, Hungarian authorities ordered Hungarian Jews living outside Budapest - roughly 500,000 - to concentrate in certain cities, usually regional government seats. When Horthy learned about the deportations, he called them "inhuman, stupid and unworthy of the Hungarian character with which the present “Hungarian”, government has sullied the Hungarian name in the eyes of the world”. Horthy wrote to his prime minister the following: “Dear Sztójay: I was aware that the Government in the given forced situation has to take many steps that I do not consider correct, and for which I cannot take responsibility. Among these matters is the handling of the Jewish question in a manner that does not correspond to the Hungarian mentality, Hungarian conditions, and, for that matter, Hungarian interests. It is clear to everyone that what among these were done by Germans or by the insistence of the Germans was not in my power to prevent, so in these matters, I was forced into passivity. As such, I was not informed in advance, or I am not fully informed now, however, I have heard recently that in many cases in inhumaneness and brutality we exceeded the Germans.” However, Sztójay ignored this and he even ramped up the pace of forced deportations of Hungarian Jews. Just before the deportations began, two Slovak Jewish prisoners, Rudolf Vrba and Alfréd Wetzler, escaped from Auschwitz and passed details of what was happening inside the camp to officials in Slovakia. This document, known as the Vrba-Wetzler Report, was quickly translated into German and passed among Jewish groups and then to Allied officials. In late June 1944, world leaders, including Pope Pius XII and American President Roosevelt, pleaded with Horthy to use his influence to stop the deportations. Roosevelt specifically threatened military retaliation if the transports were not ceased. On 2 July 1944, Horthy issued the order halting deportations on 7 July. Nevertheless, deportations to Auschwitz from cities around Budapest continued for two more days. During 8 weeks from the 15th of May to 9 July 1944, Hungarian gendarmerie officials whose members were closely linked to the antisemitic Arrow Cross, under the guidance of German SS officials, deported nearly 440,000 Jews from Hungary in more than 145 trains. Most were deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau. About 100,000 Jews from Hungary were selected for forced labor and the remainder—approximately 330,000 Jews (about 75 percent)—were murdered in the gas chambers upon arrival. This was the deadliest period at Auschwitz-Birkenau. Rudolf Höss, the commandant of the Auschwitz camp complex, begged the Hungarian authorities not to send more than one transport per day, as the camp crematoria did not have the sheer capacity to cope with the amount of bodies arriving from the gas chambers. To solve this problem, Otto Moll, director of all crematoria at Auschwitz, ordered fire pits to be dug. There, the excess people - Hungarian men, women and children - were shot in the back of their head and dropped into fire. It sometimes happened that some prisoners put up a fight or children cried. As punishment, the Nazi personnel would throw them into the burning pits alive. By the end of July 1944, the only Jewish community left in Hungary was that of Budapest, the capital. Horthy became appalled by Sztójay’s actions and demanded his removal as prime minister. However, Hitler sternly refused to do so. Eventually, in August 1944, the Germans yielded and allowed Sztójay to be replaced by General Géza Lakatos. When Horthy himself was overthrown by the Nazis in October, Sztójay was not reinstated due to poor health. He fled Hungary as the Red Army advanced, but was later captured by American forces, extradited, and sentenced to death for war crimes by a Hungarian People’s Tribunal. title: The storm system covered the USA: Pittsburgh was hit the hardest
channel_name: WHEN THE EARTH IS still ANGRY
text: A powerful storm with hurricane-force winds battered southwestern Pennsylvania, with the Pittsburgh area particularly hard hit. Wind gusts reached 115 km/h (71.3 mph) at the Pittsburgh airport, the third highest in history. In some areas, wind speeds reached 145 km/h (90 mph), equivalent to an EF-1 tornado. The storm left more than 500,000 people without power, including more than 200,000 in Allegheny County. Homes, infrastructure, and power lines were damaged. Emergency services were receiving up to 1,000 calls per minute at the peak of the storm. Schools in the region were closed or had delays in opening. Duquesne Light and West Penn Power called the storm unprecedented, stressing that it will take a long time to restore power due to the extent of the damage. The storm was part of a large system that spanned an area from Texas to the northeastern United States and caused tornadoes, hail and destruction in several states.

title: Cada vez que más lo necesitaba, él estaba con su primer amor. Muy bien, ¡mis mejores deseos!
text: On My Wedding Day Her First Love Stood in the Doorway with Tears in His Eyes. My husband gave her a look— and left me and all the guests standing there to run after her. Since that day— He was never there when I needed him most. When I was pregnant and burned so bad I couldn't move— He was taking care of his first love during her postpartum. When I fell and went into premature labor suffering from pain— He was in the hospital protecting his first love because she was sick. When our daughter became ill with a fever and was left with a permanent disability— He was busy searching for the runaway daughter of his first love. Medium. Year after year swallowing the pain. I endured for almost my entire life. Until— My son announced that he wanted to marry the daughter of my husband's first love. I died of pure rage. But when I opened my eyes again— I was back in time to the day my daughter got sick. Do you love your first love? Good. I wish you eternal happiness. Chapter 1 "Gloria Gloria wake up. Don't sleep here or you'll catch a cold..." My thoughts were a hazy mess as I slowly opened my eyes. My arms were numb and tingling, crushed under my own weight. Dim lights. The constant noise of the machines. Workers moving tirelessly. I remembered that the factory had recently imported modern foreign production lines so why did the machines in front of me look so old? A familiar voice echoed in my ears. "Oh... I don't blame you for falling asleep. Three night shifts in a row would exhaust a machine." "But Gloria, you and your husband have stable jobs. You don't need to work so hard to get ahead." I looked up. Vanessa—my best friend—was there with her jet-black hair, her young, wrinkle-free face as if she had gone back ten years overnight. My heart was beating fast. Something wasn't right. Suppressing the rising panic, I grabbed Vanessa's arm. "Vanessa… what day is it today?" Vanessa frowned in confusion. "December 3, 1966. Why do you ask ? Are you still asleep?" December 3, 1966. Today. The day that ruined my life. There was no time to waste. I tore off my work uniform as I ran out. "Vanessa, I have an emergency at home. Please tell the supervisor I'm leaving—he can deduct whatever he wants from my pay." I ran into the house. Everything was dark. The air was cold. My son slept soundly on the warm brick bed. Beside her, my daughter was writhing restlessly, her face flushed, her breathing heavy. I touched his forehead. He was burning with fever. I looked around. The only one who should have been home watching the kids—my husband Victor—was nowhere to be seen. A bitter resentment twisted in my chest. I yanked open the closet, grabbed a thick military coat, and wrapped my daughter in it as best I could to protect her from the cold. Beside me my son stirred in bed. He rubbed his sleepy eyes and muttered in annoyance. "Mom, you're making too much noise. You woke me up." "I'm leaving now. Get some rest." I turned off the kerosene lamp, picked up my daughter, and walked outside—guided only by the reflection of the snow. The roads were slippery and there were no streetlights. I fell several times before finally getting to the hospital. The doctor examined my daughter and then turned to me with a stern expression. "What kind of mother are you? Fever in children is dangerous. Why didn't you bring her in sooner? If she suffers after-effects, you'll regret it all your life." My breath caught in my throat, my voice raspy. "Will my daughter have any permanent damage?" The doctor adjusted his glasses. "Luckily you brought her in on time. The nurse will give her a drip. Once her fever goes down, she 'll be fine." I exhaled in relief. Half of my anguish dissipated. The nurse put the needle in my daughter. Little by little the feverish blush on her face disappeared and she fell asleep peacefully. While the nurse was putting her things away, she began to chat. "It's midnight and you're here alone with the girl. Where's the father?" My hands stopped. The warmth they gave me when I rubbed them vanished in an instant. Victor I remembered my past life. Before leaving for the night shift I reminded him several times. Our daughter had been sick for days. I asked him to make sure she took her medicine, to keep her warm, and to take her to the hospital if she got worse. But then the factory called him in for an emergency. Without hesitation, she ran off to work, leaving our daughter with a high fever. When I returned home his hearing was gone forever. I was torn apart inside. I took her to all the hospitals in the province. But it was already too late. Victor was an exemplary worker, a role model. In an era where collective duty took precedence over personal needs, I had no right to blame him for choosing his responsibility over his family. All I could do was drown in my own regret night after night. If I knew his fever hadn't improved, why did I trust such an irresponsible father? But this time fate had given me another chance. This time I would protect my daughter. I smiled with effort and held the nurse's curious gaze. "He's busy with work. I was the only one available." Sensing the tension, the nurse did not insist further. The next morning I went to the hospital cafeteria to buy breakfast. From afar I saw Victor carrying a Tupperware filled to the brim as he left the hospital. Was n't I supposed to be working overtime at the factory? Why was I here in the hospital? text: Imagine building the most majestic ship of the 10th century and watching it sink minutes after setting sail Welcome to the Basa Museum Home of the most spectacular shipwreck in history The Basa is a Swedish galleon built between 1626 and 1628 Loaded with 64 cannons and tons of royal ambition It was to be the emblem of the Swedish navy The largest and finest ship ever built in the country It was the pride of Sweden with which they intended to take control of the Baltic until a small miscalculation sent it straight to the bottom of the sea on its maiden voyage [Music]. The ship weighed 100 tons and its dimensions were impressive for the time: 69 m in length and 52 m from the tip of the mainmast to the keel [Music]. What happened? Basically, the Basa looked like a floating castle, but so tall and narrow that it swung like a toy. A gust of wind. A few ceremonial cannon shots and goodbye. [Music] Basa. The king insisted on providing it with two decks for the cannons. The modification altered the waterline, which was too low and that is why its lifespan was so short. On August 10, 1628, he left the port of Stockholm for the maiden voyage. 300 m later, a strong gust of wind knocked him over. Water entered through the gun ports and the ship sank within minutes with its more than 200 crew members, one of whom perished. Thirty years later, all was not lost. In 1956, wreck specialist Anders Franzen found her remains and was completely rescued. On April 24, 1961, more than 300 years later, the Basa emerged from the seabed almost intact. It was an authentic archaeological treasure frozen in time. In fact, more than 14,000 pieces were recovered after a titanic reconstruction effort. Today you can admire this beautiful and imposing ship, 98% of which is completely original, and the Basa Museum has carefully preserved it so that you can see it in all its splendor. Every year, more than a million people enter this large, multi-story hall to enjoy the gigantic wooden structure. In the Basa Museum located on Jure Garden Island, you can walk around the royal ship, as we have already mentioned, 98% of what is exhibited corresponds to the period of the ship. You will see his impressive sculptures up close. You will discover objects rescued from the seabed. and you will even learn the stories of the people who were on board that fateful day. The museum was opened in 1990 and is the most visited in all of Scandinavia. In one of its rooms, a video is projected in several languages ​​that tells the story we have just told you and the details of the rescue. Did you know that the Basa is the only ship of its kind from the 10th century that is almost entirely preserved and that the humidity and mud of Stockholm were its best allies in preserving it? The museum is open from September to May from 10 p.m. to 5 p.m. on Wednesdays until 8 a.m. and from June to August from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. in the afternoon. The entrance fee is €19 for adults and free for those under 18 and those over 65 also get a discount. So if you visit Stockholm you can't miss this unique gem in the world. The Basa Museum is waiting to tell you the story of a big mistake due to royal ambition. If you were interested in this video, give us a like and subscribe to the channel to continue accompanying us on our travels and leave us your comments. Tell us if you have already seen the Basa Museum and what you thought of this curious story. We will be waiting for you very soon in another new destination. Until then, thank you for watching this video and greetings.

title: Primera Limpieza en 11 Años de este Reanult 8 | Parte #2
text: In the previous video, I managed to unblock the Renault 8 and get it out of the corner where it has been parked for the last 11 years. And what you're seeing is the moment after so many years when it saw the light of the Sun for the first time. As you can see, it's quite dirty, covered in dust, so it needed a thorough cleaning. For this. I started by wetting it with a Kärcher pressure washer and then I started to do the rims. For the rims I used a special spray and a rag and scrubbed carefully. Once the rims were done, I soaped everything up with this hose attachment, which is a brush that comes with a small soap reservoir and as the water comes out, the brush rotates. Once soaped, I ran water over it again and dried it with a microfiber towel to remove any limescale stains. Once dry, I applied a little polish all over the bodywork and, as you can see, the results are already starting to show. The car looks much better now. Like for more videos of this Renault 8.

text: We are the generation that talks the most about their emotions, the generation that has normalized feeling depressed, stressed and anxious… but do you think it has served any purpose? The reality is that we are getting worse. In the last 20 years, the consumption of antidepressants has tripled, suicides have increased by 20%, and psychological and mental health professionals are overwhelmed. Today I'm going to make a different video, it's possibly going to be something that will generate some controversy, but I'm going to give my opinion trying to maintain absolute respect for both the people who suffer and the professionals who treat them. You may not know it yet, but hundreds of thousands of people around the world have already experienced, first-hand, the definitive solution to put an end to most of their emotional suffering. It's time to put an end to this real social problem once and for all. Let's get down to business. “Expressing your emotions doesn’t solve them, it reinforces them.” This is my humble opinion, but there are many influential people in the world of psychology and personal growth who already spoke about this years ago, such as David Hawkins, psychiatrist and doctor of philosophy, in his book Letting Go, where he argues that expressing emotions only lightens their burden enough, at that moment, to be able to remove them from consciousness, but that it tends to spread that feeling and give it greater energy. He also explains that “if we dump our negative feelings on others, they will experience it as an attack, and in turn, they will be forced to suppress, express, or escape from those feelings; therefore, the expression of negativity results in the deterioration and destruction of relationships.” Not everything is negative, it is true that the social movement towards the normalization of emotional problems has achieved something very important, that these issues are spoken about openly and are taken into consideration much more than before. But is it enough to talk about them? What's the point really? According to Hawkins, if all we do is express our discomfort, we are making the problem bigger, and this seems to be what is happening. It is also well known that repressing emotions is equally harmful, but it is sad that today, in most personal growth and psychology channels, people in the comments only celebrate feeling understood. I’m not saying it’s not great to find someone who understands your feelings, but do you think that feeling of “wow, finally someone understands me” has ever solved anything? In my opinion, the only thing that reinforces it is the normalization of the problem, thinking, okay, I'm not the only one, what happens to me is normal. When what makes your life difficult becomes understandable and normal, it stops being a problem and becomes part of you, I would dare say that there is even a certain feeling of pride, you defend your suffering tooth and nail, and instead of looking for solutions, what you do is look for validation and project your situation onto others. I'm not saying it's not normal, or the easy way out, it's just much more comfortable to try to feel understood than to actually put the problem on the table and act. What is truly alarming is that society is increasingly losing the values ​​of effort and improvement, and ideals are being destroyed in pursuit of “respect” for the disadvantaged. To give some practical examples, although the problem goes much further... today you can no longer repeat a year at school, all tournaments have consolation trophies, and it seems that the dream of every Spaniard is that the president in power provides aid for public transport instead of having to find a way to get ahead. Obviously the latter is an exaggeration, but it's the feeling I've had for years: it's fashionable to complain, to play the victim and to express discomfort, and it seems like it's an insult to have to work and work on yourself to get ahead. Leaving aside the economic situation of our country, which I leave to the experts (and unfortunately it seems that the government is missing a few), I am going to give you a hypothetical example. Imagine for a moment, that one day you wake up and you can't move your legs. Suddenly you can't walk or do what you were used to doing, your life takes a 180 degree turn. At that point you have 3 options. The first option is to give up, accept your limitations, consider yourself an unfortunate person, a victim of your situation or of society. If you continue down this path, you will probably look for others to adapt to your situation, and complaining and demanding will become a habit in your life. Everything will seem like an impediment to you. The second option is to try to compensate for your limitations through effort, strengthen your upper body, achieve everything that can help you live a normal life, seek help wherever possible and strive to find things that you can do without needing your legs and that make you feel fulfilled and complete. I know it's difficult, maybe it's a strength that not everyone has, or maybe not everyone has the ideal circumstances to do it, but at least I think it should be something to aspire to. This type of attitude is what has allowed many people to go so far and have a full life. People like Isidre Esteve, who after a serious motorcycle accident, redirected his life to continue doing what made him happy. Or like Alex Roca, the first person with a disability to finish a marathon, who some time ago said on a television program that he does what he does because it makes him happy, and that he wants to be a role model so that people, whatever their limitations (which we all have) fight for their dreams. People like them make me feel small, honestly. From here, my

title: Estudiantes y Paraguas || La Revolución de Los Paraguas de 2014
text: The Umbrella Wars, also known as the Umbrella Movement, was a series of protests that took place in Hong Kong between September and December 2014. This movement emerged as a response to the growing dissatisfaction of Hong Kong citizens with the Beijing government and the limitation of their democratic rights. Its origins date back to a decision by the Chinese central government, which announced that the elections for Hong Kong's next chief executive, scheduled for 2017, would be controlled by a nominating committee, leaving voters with very few real options. The name "Umbrella Wars" comes from the symbolic use of the umbrella during the demonstrations. From the beginning of the protests, participants used umbrellas to protect themselves not only from the rain, but also from police aggression, which included the use of tear gas and other repressive tactics. Umbrellas became a visual emblem of the movement, symbolizing the struggle for democracy and civil rights in Hong Kong. Furthermore, its use represented a peaceful form of resistance, contrasting with the violence that the protesters faced. As the protests progressed, occupation camps were formed in several areas of Hong Kong, the most notable being Admiralty, which became the nerve center of the demonstrations. Thousands of people joined the cause, which sought to demand true democracy and the protection of human rights in the region. The protests were organized mainly by students and young people, who used social media and digital platforms to mobilize more people. Protesters also held various activities, such as public debates and forums, to discuss their demands and raise awareness about the political situation in Hong Kong. Chinese authorities and the Hong Kong government responded to the protests with evictions and repression. Despite the pressure, the movement's leaders remained committed to continuing the protests peacefully. title: UN DÍA A LA VEZ: Mini hábitos que pueden salvarte 🦋

But it does offer you something real: mini habits. Steps so small they almost don't seem like steps, but they can make a difference. If the navigation is confusing or the site loads slowly, they're likely to leave before making a purchase. So let's start with the most important thing: optimizing your store to improve sales. It is crucial. If you want to increase sales, you need to make sure your store is easy to navigate and offers an engaging shopping experience. Conversion rate optimization, or CRO, is a technique that focuses on improving the usability of your store and ensuring that users can easily find what they're looking for. Another impediment to selling more may be the following. text: Adriana discovers the secret will that will bring down Úrsula. What if the most dangerous enemy wasn't a stranger, but your own hidden sister? Adriana never imagined that the Little House—her refuge and symbol of everything she had ever loved—held an ancient secret that could change the fate of the Savage Valley forever. While Úrsula wove her web of deceit to steal Adriana’s home, her family, and even Rafael’s love, an unexpected revelation would change everything: a forgotten will, a lost diary, and an identity buried in ashes. Just when the auction seemed to seal the final betrayal, Adriana, along with Mercedes and a mysterious ally—the Duke’s hidden brother—unleashed the truth in public, bringing with it the downfall of Victoria, José Luis, and the false heiress who had been preparing her revenge for years. Intrigue, family betrayals, shouted confessions, and a devastating revelation that explains everything: the past returns like a whirlwind to destroy carefully constructed lies. Are you ready to discover the true story of the Savage Valley and witness the final battle for justice, love, and legacy? So don't move, because this is much more than a drama: it's the outcome you were waiting for... and that you will never forget. He looked for Bernardo, his loyal friend, the only one he could fully trust. She poured out her fears, the anguish of knowing she was cornered. "I can't stand it, Bernardo," she whispered, tears blurring her eyes. "Watching Victoria, the woman who destroyed my sister, about to take my place, to take everything we held dear, is agony." Powerlessness consumed her, a slow fire that threatened to reduce her to ashes. But, as always, a spark of resistance flickered within her. Maybe, just maybe, not all was lost. There had to be a way to stop Victoria and José Luis from getting away with it. A way to unearth the truth, to expose their lies before it was too late. Meanwhile, in another corner of the estate, Atanasio continued his subtle and disconcerting dance. His movements were ambiguous, his closeness to Victoria, increasingly noticeable, confused everyone. Victoria, blinded by the belief that he was José Luis’s new right-hand man, saw him as a potential ally, someone she had to win over. She didn’t know that Atanasio wasn’t seeking to win her favor, but information. She didn’t know that the man with whom she shared calculated confidences and forced smiles was the brother of the late Duke, the man who had his own secret agenda: to discover the truth about his brother’s death and the usurper who took his place. Atanasio watched, listened, and wove his own invisible web, waiting for the opportune moment to strike. Victoria, in her arrogance, was blind to the true intentions of those around her. The tension in the air was palpable, especially between Adriana and Ursula. The young woman, unable to contain her resentment and concern for Pedrito, openly confronted Úrsula, accusing her of manipulating the child. The argument escalated quickly, culminating in a painful confrontation in front of Rafael. What hurt Adriana the most were not Úrsula's words, but Rafael's reaction. Far from defending her, from seeking the truth, he saw jealousy in her words. Pure and simple envy And he positioned himself against her. "Adriana, you're being irrational," he had told her, his eyes cold. "Úrsula is only trying to help Pedrito. Your jealousy makes no sense." Each word was a blow, a cruel reminder of the distance that seemed to grow between them, fueled by Ursula's machinations. Adriana retreated, hurt, humiliation burning her cheeks. Jealousy? Yes, perhaps there was jealousy. Jealousy of the ease with which Úrsula moved in her world, of the way she seemed to enchant everyone, even Rafael. But it was something deeper than simple romantic jealousy. It was a visceral distrust, a feeling that Úrsula was a threat to the stability of his family, to the peace of the valley. And Rafael couldn't, or wouldn't, see it. While the drama unfolded in and around the Casa Grande, Leonardo received an unexpected visitor. Barbara appeared at his door, showing genuine concern for his health. The gesture moved Leonardo, who had been feeling lonely and dejected. Barbara's kindness lit a small spark of hope in his heart. Perhaps, he thought, it was still possible for something to blossom between them. It was a ray of light in the darkness that enveloped him. But the darkness lurked, and Victoria was in charge of spreading it. Without a hint of remorse, he told Luisa his decision: he would put the Little House up for sale. That meant the end of Luisa's stay in the valley. Luisa's face fell. The Little House was her home, the place where she had served Adriana's family for years, where she kept so many memories. Úrsula, always astute, didn't waste any time. He took advantage of Luisa's vulnerability, offering her false sympathy, a shoulder to cry on. He knew that Luisa was one of the people closest to Adriana. Winning over the maid meant gaining valuable information and, in the process, further isolating Adriana. Later, Ursula shared her progress with Victoria. "Luisa is in the palm of my hand, Aunt," she said with a satisfied smile. "She feels lost, vulnerable. She's started confiding in me little things about Adriana, about the estate. " Victoria listened, her eyes shining with pride. "You're doing magnificently, Ursula. You're winning everyone over. José Luis trusts you, the staff adores you, even Atanasio seems intrigued by you." He paused, his expression darkening slightly. "Although Adriana is still an obstacle A thorn in my side." Ursula frowned. "I don't understand your intensity, Aunt. Why do you hate me so much? I haven't done anything to you. " Victoria looked at her, weighing her words. Was this the moment? title: End of an Era: Bell and Boeing Conclude CV-22 Osprey Production for the U.S. Air Force!
text: Welcome to the Titan TAR channel. Today we have a topic to discuss about Bell and Boeing conclude CV 22 Osprey production for the US Air Force. Don't miss the chance to join us and share your opinions with us subscribing and liking to grow our community. Become a member of our channel and evolve your rank. Beltextron incorporated, a subsidiary of Textron Incorporated and Boeing recently celebrated a major milestone in military aviation history. the imminent conclusion of the CV 22 program of record for the US Air Force. This significant achievement was marked during a ceremony at the Bell Amarillo Assembly Center in Texas on April 18th, honoring years of innovation and collaboration in creating a groundbreaking aircraft. The CV22, a specialized variant of the V22 Osprey, stands as a testament to advanced tiltrotor technology designed for special operations. It merges the vertical takeoff and landing capabilities of a helicopter with the speed and range of a fixed-wing aircraft. As the first tiltrotor aircraft introduced into military service, the CV 22 has redefined air mobility and operational flexibility. Serving across multiple branches of the US armed forces and setting new standards in military aviation, Bell highlighted the US Air Force's leadership in completing its program of record for the CV22, which incorporates enhanced NEL designs for improved performance. The final aircraft in this historic program is slated for delivery in the coming months. Reflecting on this achievement, Elden Mezer, Bellev 22 program director emphasized the significance of this milestone, stating that the transition from production to fleetwide sustainment marks the beginning of a new chapter for the aircraft's legacy. The CV 22 Osprey has earned its place in history through its critical role in numerous high-profile missions. These include the longest nighttime hostage rescue in the Department of Defense's history and the evacuation of 194 individuals from the US Embassy in Baghdad. Its versatility extends to long range medical evacuations, including operations requiring precision landings on moving naval vessels far offshore. As production concludes, Bell and Boeing reaffirm their commitment to supporting the CV22's operational excellence through sustainment and upgrades while production of other Osprey variants for the US Marine Corps and Navy continues. title: Tomás y la Luciérnaga Dorada | Cuento Infantil Mágico para Dormir | Historia para Niños
text: In the quiet little town of Luminaria, little Tomás can't sleep. Outside, the night shines with millions of stars, but he feels an emptiness in his heart. Suddenly, a warm light flickers outside her window. —What could that beautiful light be? —Hi, Thomas. I am Lia, the golden firefly. I have sought you out because you need brightness in your dreams. Tomás leaves his room and follows Lía to the garden. There he discovers glowing flowers, whimsically shaped bushes, and a path of luminous petals leading into the darkness. I've never seen anything so magical. —This is the enchanted garden; Each petal holds a forgotten wish. Come and see. At the end of the path, a glass bridge appears to float on a stream of liquid light. Lía warns Tomás that he must cross it with courage and explains that each step reflects her fears. —Don’t be afraid, Thomas. The bridge mirror will only show what the heart holds. —What if I see my worst nightmares? —Then cross with the certainty that you are stronger than them. After crossing, they reach a clearing where a large golden oak stands. At its base, an ancient chest waits to be opened. Lía explains that therein lies the gift for those who overcome their fears: the spark of confidence. “The chest belongs to me,” says Thomas, “ because I have faced my fears.” —Open it with a sigh of hope. Tomas takes the spark of confidence in his hand and feels his chest fill with calm and joy. Lia guides him back to the threshold of his house, reminding him that the light will always live inside him. —Thank you, Lia. Now I know that the magic is within me. -Thanks to you. You will always shine, Tomás. Good night.

title: Americans advised to prepare for start of Real ID enforcement
text: The deadline to get your real ID before enforcement starts is less than a week from today, May 7th. If you don't have a real ID or a different federallymandated form of identification, like a passport, you could face delays getting through airport security. A San Diego International is telling passengers to get to the airport early starting next Wednesday just in case. The airport plans to have extra staff on hand to handle any concerns that passengers have over Real ID. Congress passed the Real ID Act back in 2005.

title: When Did Compliance Become a Trap?
text: When did compliance become a trap? When did compliance stop being about protection and start being about control? Compliance was never meant to be this. It was meant to hold safety. It was meant to ensure fairness. It was meant to protect people, not punish them. Now we have compliance tests where the language is deliberately vague. The answers are based on preference, not principle. And the real message is you must comply to prove you're worthy of staying. But here's the truth. Real compliance is not a performance. It's a vibration. It's clarity. It's coherence. It's integrity and structure, not punishment by semantics. So let's stop designing systems that trick people into obedience. Let's build frameworks that teach people to stand in truth. Because the future of governance is not about memorizing rules. title: Bullied for Winning a Scholarship… But Allah Proved Everyone Wrong | Islamic Story | Believers Diary
text: Hello, my name is Lyanna. A few years ago, something happened at school that really shook my confidence. Since childhood, I had always been a good student, the teacher's favorite, always buried in books. I finished my homework on time, scored excellent marks on exams, and was proud of it. My friends knew how seriously I took my studies. Fortunately, they accepted me as I was. So, whenever they needed help with their studies, we would study together and even have fun. Everything was going well. But one day, things suddenly changed. One day, our principal announced that students who achieved the highest results in their grade would receive a full scholarship, meaning all their educational expenses would be covered. Everyone wanted to win it, but most didn't put in extra effort. Many continued as usual without working harder. But I started studying twice as much. I knew my parents could really use the extra support and I wanted them to be proud of me. Gradually, I spent less time with friends, canceled plans, and focused entirely on my studies. At first, my friends didn't seem to mind, but over time, they started becoming distant. I didn't realize it, at least not until it was too late. Finally, the day of the award ceremony arrived. The entire school gathered in the auditorium. One by one, the winners's names were announced. My name wasn't being called and I started feeling extremely nervous. I feared that maybe I hadn't worked hard enough and that all my efforts had been in vain. My hope was slowly fading. Then when it was time to announce the last name I had already accepted, it's over. But then the principal said, "My name." I practically jumped out of my seat with joy. However, that happiness didn't last long. A classmate turned around and said with irritation, "You don't deserve this. Your family is rich. You didn't have to sacrifice anything to get this." I was shocked. The entire class heard it, and I wished I could disappear. The truth was, I was never rich. But no one knew that my father had undergone multiple major surgeries after a terrible car accident. He had lost his job and was unable to work. My mother had spent all our family savings on his treatment and we were struggling to survive. This scholarship meant everything to me. But that one comment felt like a dagger to my heart. I started doubting myself. Had I really worked hard enough or had I just taken an opportunity away from someone more deserving. I felt ashamed as if I had been exposed as a fraud. What happened next? I never imagined. Before being a top student had brought my friends closer, but now it pushed everyone away. Students started talking behind my back, making fun of me in class whenever I answered a question. It felt like I was being punished for who I had always been. People at school made sure I knew they thought I didn't deserve the scholarship. I felt so heartbroken that I even considered giving it back. At school, it seemed better to lose the money than to lose my friends. But when I got home, I knew I couldn't do that to my family. My provision was from Allah and no one could take it away. I was so miserable that one of my favorite teachers noticed and asked me why I was so quiet. As soon as I started explaining, I broke down in tears. She listened carefully and then said, "Do you think what people say about you is what truly matters? What really matters is how Allah sees you. If you work hard in a halal way and people falsely accuse you, know that Allah is on your side. I remain silent. Then she continued, "Allah says in the Quran, so whoever does an Adam's weight of good will see it." Surah Aala 7. She smiled and added, "If someone else was more deserving, they would have received it. But you were chosen because you earned it." And that is still true today. From that day on, I stopped worrying about what others thought. Within a few weeks, people moved on to other things and the gossip faded. But the most important lesson I learned was when Allah grants a blessing, some people will always be jealous. Eventually, my closest friends found out about my father's situation. They understood why the scholarship was so important to me, and we started reconnecting. This experience taught me a valuable lesson. People's opinions do not define the truth. The truth is what we believe about ourselves and how Allah values us. Dear friends, we should never let others words discourage us. Instead, we should put our trust in Allah. text: The myth that humans only use 10% of their brain has been widely spread through the public and media for a long time, but it is scientifically unfounded. The origin of this myth comes from the 19th century American psychologist William James who noted that humans use only a portion of their potential. Afterwards, the expression “use only 10%” appeared in self-development books in the 1930s and became established as a fact, and was often used in popular culture, including the movie Lucy. However, modern neuroscience research shows that we use multiple areas of the brain simultaneously. As a result of brain imaging such as MRI, it has been confirmed that several parts of the brain are activated through simple actions or thoughts. In reality, if 90% of your brain is idle, there shouldn't be any problems when that area is damaged, but in reality, even a small brain injury can cause significant disability. Experts emphasize that the claim that only 10% of the brain is used has no scientific basis and that the brain is always active as a whole.

title: The Night Stalker: It Hunts in the Dark, It Feeds on Fear… #horrorstories #terrifyingtales #horror
text: It hunts in the dark. It feeds on fear. And tonight, it's coming for you. Villagers whispered about the creature that prowled after sunset. A shadowy beast with glowing red eyes and claws sharp enough to slice through bone. No one who saw it lived to tell the tale. But Alex didn't believe the stories until tonight. As Alex walked home alone, he heard it, a low growl from the shadows. He turned just in time to see the creature step into the moonlight. Its elongated limbs ended in razor- sharp talons, and its mouth stretched impossibly wide, revealing rows of jagged teeth. Alex ran faster than he ever had before, but the creature was relentless. Every step echoed louder behind him, closer. He could feel its hot breath on his neck as it lunged forward, its claws grazing his jacket. Just as Alex reached the edge of the woods, the creature tackled him to the ground. Its guttural roar drowned out his screams as its gaping mud descended upon him. By morning, all that remained were shredded clothes and claw marks deep in the earth. And now it waits for its next victim.

title: May 1st: The Day Workers Changed History
text: Why is May 1st more than just a date? On May 1st, 1886, thousands of workers in Chicago took to the streets, demanding what seemed radical at the time — 8 hours for work, 8 for rest, and 8 for life. Their protest was peaceful — until it wasn’t. The Haymarket Affair turned into chaos. Lives were lost. But their courage lit a fire that spread worldwide. It took years, but eventually — the world listened. We celebrate May 1st to remember a day when workers stood up — and never sat back down. It’s the workers’ day — carved into history, carried by memory.

title: How to master IELTS Speaking cue card
text: Welcome. In this guide, we're going to talk about how to master the IELTS speaking Q card, also known as part two of the speaking test. This part often makes candidates nervous because you have just one minute to prepare and then you have to speak for up to two minutes. But don't worry, with the right strategy, you can speak confidently, stay on topic, and impress the examiner. Here's how it works. The examiner gives you a topic on a task card, and you get one minute to prepare. You can take notes during that time. Then you must speak continuously for 1 to two minutes. So what's the best way to prepare? First, use the one minute prep time wisely. Don't try to write full sentences. Just note down keywords and ideas. Focus on the main points given on the card. These will guide your response. Next, use the PPF method, past, present, and future. This technique helps you expand your answer naturally. For example, if the Q card says, describe a person who has influenced you, you could talk about how you met them in the past, how they influence you now, and what impact they might have on your future. Also, structure matters. Try this simple format. Start with an introduction. Give some background. Tell the main story or experience. Then wrap up with a conclusion. Think of it as telling a mini story with a beginning, middle, and end. Fluency is key. You don't need perfect grammar or fancy vocabulary, but you do need to keep going without long pauses. If you get stuck, use filler phrases like, "That's an interesting question to buy time." Naturally, vocabulary variety will also help. Instead of repeating the same words like nice or good, use more descriptive language. Practice using words related to common topics like people, places, events, and experiences. Don't worry if you go slightly off topic or forget a point. The examiner is listening for your ability to communicate, not just for perfect answers. Here's a tip. Practice with a timer. Give yourself one minute to prepare, then speak for two minutes. Record yourself and listen for areas to improve your pace, clarity, and structure. Finally, remember to stay relaxed and natural. Smile if it helps you feel more confident. The examiner wants you to do well. Think of the test as a conversation, not an interrogation. With practice, the Qard section can actually become one of your strongest parts of the test. Thanks for listening. If you found this helpful, be sure to check out our next guide on IELTS speaking part three where we handle abstract questions and opinion based discussion. Good luck with your LS preparation.

title: Did Lee Jong Suk Cross the Line? The Reason Netflix Dropped Him!
text: Amid the explosive wave of K-dramas on OTT platforms, Lee Jong Suk’s name remains solid — not just for his striking visuals, but also for his weighty roles like Park Chang Ho in Big Mouth. Yet behind this glow lies a strange absence: for the past six years, he has had no involvement in any original Netflix production — a rare situation for an A-list Korean actor. Recently, the possible cause of this absence has emerged — through a shocking accusation that has ignited debate across social media. A Long Silence and the Big Question from Fans On August 8, what began as a casual forum post on Koreaboo — “Why hasn’t Lee Jong Suk starred in a Netflix original yet?” — quickly turned into a media frenzy. A netizen claiming to be a former staff member on the See You Again production team alleged that Lee Jong Suk was originally cast in the leading role of the 2018 Netflix project but abruptly pulled out just one day before the first script reading, causing the entire project to be canceled. Netflix issued only a brief statement at the time: “Things didn’t go as expected, so we had to change plans.” But now, the reasons behind the cancellation are being re-examined in light of these claims — and they paint a troubling picture. Root Cause of the Fallout – Star Syndrome or Professional Decision? According to the whistleblower, Lee Jong Suk demanded an “unimaginably high” appearance fee for See You Again. When Netflix declined to meet his demands, he allegedly backed out of the role at the last minute, without any apology or sense of accountability. “I lost my job,” the accuser stated. “Equipment was ready, scripts were printed, and the cast had been notified. He ruined everything with one decision.” Even more concerning, this isn’t the first time Lee has been accused of delaying commitments. The same individual claimed that Lee Jong Suk had previously postponed confirmation for dramas like Come and Hug Me and The Witch: Part 1 – The Subversion, causing scheduling chaos for everyone involved. Is this a case of meticulous script selection — or the manifestation of unchecked star syndrome? Netflix and the Quiet Power of Industry Standards Netflix is known for innovation and flexibility, but it also runs on an ecosystem of strict professionalism. Ethical behavior, punctuality, and reliability are non-negotiable. Though there’s been no official blacklist announcement, the fact that Lee Jong Suk has been completely absent from the platform’s original content for six years speaks volumes. Instead of making public judgments, Netflix may be practicing a “silent exclusion” — quietly distancing itself from artists deemed high-risk. In the entertainment world, unofficial blacklists are often more powerful than any formal declaration. The Court of Public Opinion: Victim or Villain? Public opinion remains deeply divided. Many netizens have expressed skepticism toward the anonymous accusation, citing the possibility of fabricated or exaggerated claims intended to smear the actor’s reputation. “He wasn’t under contract — he had the right to withdraw,” one user argued. Supporters also point to Lee Jong Suk’s continued success with hits like Big Mouth and While You Were Sleeping, suggesting that his reputation within the industry remains strong. However, critics question his ongoing silence. By choosing not to respond to the mounting accusations, is Lee Jong Suk risking further erosion of trust — especially in an era where “cancel culture” thrives on ambiguity? OTT Isn’t Always a Golden Ticket Another perspective raised in Lee Jong Suk’s defense centers on the uncertain future of OTT content. While streaming platforms have grown in popularity, success is far from guaranteed. Even Netflix has seen some high-profile flops, and competitors like Disney+, Coupang Play, and VING face their own challenges. For a top-tier actor like Lee Jong Suk, careful selection of roles is not only wise but necessary. Some argue that his withdrawal from See You Again may have stemmed from creative misalignment rather than greed. In that context, walking away could be seen as a professional — even principled — move. Conclusion: An Unfinished Chapter The Lee Jong Suk–Netflix saga remains unresolved. With the actor’s team yet to issue any official response, and the original whistleblower remaining anonymous, the truth is difficult to verify. But one thing is clear: the incident has reignited important conversations about professionalism, accountability, and power dynamics in the Korean entertainment industry. Can a star remain immune to industry standards at the peak of fame? And if a past mistake was made — perhaps out of immaturity or misjudgment — can time and success truly wash it away? Lee Jong Suk may continue to soar without Netflix, but the 2018 controversy still casts a long shadow over his legacy. In the end, what fans may crave more than another blockbuster role is something simpler: an honest word, a thoughtful explanation. In showbiz, sometimes a sincere apology speaks louder than any performance.

title: Atatürk Hiç Doğmasaydı? Türkiye’nin Kaderi Nasıl Değişirdi? - Alternatif Tarih Çizgisi
text: Sometimes history changes direction with the presence of a single person, and sometimes, in the absence of that person... A completely different destiny is written. What if... Mustafa Kemal Atatürk had never been born? How would the history of Türkiye and even the world be shaped? At the beginning of the 20th century, the Ottoman Empire entered a serious disintegration process. The state, which was defeated in the Balkan Wars, suffered great military and economic devastation following the Tripoli and World Wars. After the Armistice of Mudros , the Allied Powers began occupying Ottoman territory. Istanbul was de facto occupied. The Greek advance began on the Aegean coast. French and Italian forces spread out to the south. In a scenario where Atatürk was not born, a leadership vacuum would have occurred. During this process, a central authority that would unite local resistance could not be established. The Istanbul Government did not show effective resistance against the occupations . As a result, occupation movements soon became permanent. Mustafa Kemal's arrival in Samsun and the congresses that followed did not take place. Therefore, the Erzurum and Sivas Congresses were not held, and a national resistance spirit could not be organized in Anatolia. In this environment, the provisions of the Treaty of Sevres were implemented step by step. Western Anatolia was given to Greece. In the south, Adana and its surroundings were left under French mandate. Istanbul was handed over to an international administration. In the east, an independent Armenia was established. A small and weak local government centered in Ankara was created in Central Anatolia. However, this structure did not receive international recognition. The people of Anatolia had to live in fragments under various mandates. With the implementation of the Treaty of Sevres, various mandate administrations were established in Anatolia. England dominated Southeastern Anatolia, France dominated Çukurova and the Syrian border, and Italy dominated the Mediterranean coast. During this period, Turkish identity weakened. Regional powers strengthened their authority in their own regions by forming collaborative administrations . Education, law and administrative structures began to take shape under the control of occupying states . Turkish has been gradually pushed into the background in the public sphere. Western pressure on Islamic institutions increased, and the caliphate's influence became largely symbolic. In the north and east of Anatolia, Armenian and Greek population mobility increased, and the Turkish population retreated to the inner regions. In the absence of Ataturk, the Republic of Türkiye was never established. A modern legal system could not be established in the 1920s. Sharia courts continued to exist. Regulations such as the Civil Code were not made. Women could not advance in terms of education and social rights. Unity in education could not be achieved; Different curricula were implemented in different regions. Arabic letters continued to be used instead of the new Turkish alphabet. Because industrialization was not encouraged, Anatolia could not leave the agricultural society. The concepts of democracy, secularism and independence did not become widespread. Thus, Türkiye transformed into a structure similar to other mandate governments in the Middle East throughout the 20th century . Today, in this alternative scenario, the Anatolian lands are divided into several small states. As an international city, Istanbul has remained under the administration of different states. Greek influence is evident in Western Anatolia. There is a weak Turkish administration in Central Anatolia, but its influence in the international arena is limited. The level of economic development is parallel to neighboring Middle Eastern countries. Education and health services are inadequate. International achievements in the field of science and technology have not been achieved. An independent line cannot be followed in foreign policy and one remains under the influence of major powers . Turkish identity, on the other hand, remained weakened between local identities and different cultural influences . The fate of a nation sometimes changes with one person . If Mustafa Kemal Atatürk had not been born, Anatolia would not have experienced a revival. A people would not be able to learn the meaning of freedom, modernity and independence . We must not forget that changing the history of a nation is sometimes possible with just one person's presence .
