title: İnsanları Etkilemek için Yapman Gereken 5 Şey! #motivation
text: When you enter a room, would you want everyone to listen to you attentively? The answer may be in your posture, not in your voice. Start with a strong question. You should be ready to not only speak but also to attract attention. Questions open the doors of your mind. Don't forget your body language. Even though the words come out of your mouth, what really tells you is your posture. Keep your shoulders open, your eyes clear, your voice calm. Talk less. Be concise. The more words, the more confusion. Giving a message in a simple sentence creates trust. Remember to establish a connection. Asking and listening are also art of communication. Sometimes a pause says more than a sentence. Make the last sentence unforgettable. People often remember the feeling at the end of what you said. That's why your closing should be simple but striking.

title: Hayatına Pozitiflik Katacak Basit Meditasyon Sırları!
text: Meditation is a simple yet effective practice that enhances your mental well-being and helps you view life positively. Before starting, find a quiet area where you won’t be disturbed. Sit or lie down in a position where you feel comfortable and secure. Wait for a time when your mind is open and willing to try. Relax. Keep your back straight, shoulders loose. Close your eyes or keep them slightly open and turn inward. Focus on your breath: Take a deep breath in through your nose and exhale through your mouth. If your mind wanders or thoughts arise, gently return to your breath without judgment. Our goal isn’t to silence the mind but to observe thoughts! Maintain your posture: Keep your head upright, arms relaxed. Release tension from your toes to the top of your head. Try to repeat daily for at least 3 minutes. Especially in the mornings…

title: Что нового в Citroën C5 Aircross 2025? Полный обзор
text: Citroën is not standing still - the French have been working on a complete renewal of their model range for several years now. It all started with the budget Citroën C3, followed by the C3 Aircross, the upgraded C4 and C4 X. And now, finally, it’s the turn of the flagship! The new Citroen C5 Aircross is a crossover in which the brand has collected all the best things it has been working on recently. The new generation is not just a “restyling”, but a real reboot: fresh design, innovative technologies, even more comfort and space, and, importantly, a wide range of power plants. Here you have a classic hybrid, a plug-in, and for the first time a fully electric version! After months of spy photos, insiders and concepts, the new C5 Aircross has officially debuted. It remains in the familiar C-SUV segment, but is completely new – both in appearance and inside. With this crossover, Citroen seems to be putting a bold end to the large-scale brand renewal program. Let's start with the fact that the new Citroen C5 Aircross has become noticeably larger. The transition to the STLA platform from Stellantis allowed the brand to create more harmonious proportions and give the crossover a more solid look. The length is now 4652 mm – 150 mm more than its predecessor, and the width has increased to 1902 mm. The wheelbase has been extended to 2784 mm, an increase of 60 mm – and all this extra length has benefited second-row passengers, who now have more knee room. The height of the crossover is 1.66 m - slightly lower than before, but this helps reduce aerodynamic drag. The ground clearance is 200 mm. The Citroen C5 Aircross crossover has changed dramatically and now looks completely new. Its design now resembles last year's pre-production concept more than the previous model. The smooth lines of the body have given way to more prominent edges. The car received a high hood, powerful bumpers and expressive fenders, giving it an aggressive look. In the center of the front section is the updated brand logo, and the signature three-point light graphics are made in the form of thin horizontal LED elements that visually expand the body. The Matrix headlights are connected by a black glossy strip. On the side, there is a smooth line from the bonnet to the stern and a slightly sloping roof line – all to reduce drag and preserve space inside. Additional air intakes and spoilers enhance efficiency. The rear part repeats the front part in style – with a glossy black insert and a vertical trunk door. The narrow top and aerodynamic elements on the pillars emphasize the width and silhouette of the model. 20-inch wheels complete the look. Although this crossover cannot boast a record aerodynamic drag coefficient, thanks to carefully thought-out design solutions, the drag coefficient was reduced from 0.84 to 0.75. This gives an additional 30 km of highway range for the electric version. For the first time, the model received a fully electric version – Citroen ë-C5 Aircross. However, the manufacturer has not abandoned hybrid solutions: the crossover is also available as a mild hybrid and a plug-in hybrid. But there will no longer be purely petrol or diesel versions in the new generation , at least for the EU market. Under the hood of the new Citroen C5 Aircross Hybrid is a 1.2-litre, three-cylinder turbocharged petrol engine. It is accompanied by a small electric motor with a peak power of 28 hp, integrated into a six-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The total capacity of the system is 145 hp. and, thanks to a 0.9 kWh lithium-ion battery located under the driver's seat, it can operate in electric mode for up to 50 km in certain situations. The battery is charged automatically during braking or deceleration. According to the car manufacturer, the hybrid development provides a total range of about 900 km according to the WLTP cycle. The new C5 Aircross plug-in hybrid is equipped with a powertrain consisting of a 1.6-liter four-cylinder petrol engine producing 150 hp. and an electric motor with a capacity of 92 kW (125 hp). The total combined power is 195 horsepower. It is equipped with a 7-speed automatic transmission and a front-wheel drive system. title: Cuauhtémoc minimiza éxito de Jardine: "Con ese equipo, cualquiera dirige”
text: Cuautemo Blanco downplayed the work of América's technical director, Andrés Yardine. In statements offered on the Shagi Martínez podcast, the iconic former Águilas striker affirmed that the Azulcrema team's recent achievements are primarily the result of the financial investment made by club owner Emilio Azcárraga, who has built a roster with high- quality players. " With the team he has, any coach can manage," Blanco stated, thus downplaying the Brazilian coach's work. The Azul Crema idol emphasized the financial investment made by Azcárraga, which, in his view, has been decisive in the team's success, suggesting that the abundance of talent makes the coaching staff's job easier. Despite this, the CAU did recognize Yardine's ability to manage a locker room with multiple figures and achieve effective group cohesion.

title: 🎵 *PERO TE VI* – Canción Original de GramolaIA | Estreno 2025 💔
text: Today I wanted to be alone, to walk along the docks, along the damp flagstones of the port, to look over the red and silver reflections of the sleeping ships. Just... Listen to the squawking of the seagulls, feel their slow and safe flapping of wings airing the sheets of my soul. But I saw you sitting on the dock, wrapped in a cloud of silence, looking at the bottom of the sea. It was a mirage of you that I recreated in my mind. I can't forget you. I wanted to be alone this time, to see the day die behind the horizon. I breathe deeply and your perfume fills my lungs. I continue walking aimlessly, feeling full of your absence. But I saw you sitting on the dock, wrapped in a cloud of silence looking at the bottom of the sea. It was a mirage of you that I recreated in my mind. I can't forget you . What I do? What am I doing? Why do I sigh when I see you barefoot stepping on the gold of the beach if you are not there? But I saw you sitting on the dock, wrapped in a cloud of silence looking at the bottom of the sea. It was a mirage of you that I recreated in my mind. I can't forget you . Today I wanted to be alone and yet I see you everywhere . I hear you in every voice and I wait for you in every dawn...

text: Boil the potatoes in their jackets until soft. Season the potatoes with salt, pepper, sweet paprika and garlic. Place the potatoes on the oven rack and preheat it to 180°C. Chop the parsley, prepare a strip of butter and a few slices of lemon. Place a piece of salmon on aluminum foil, season with salt and pepper, add butter and a slice of lemon, then wrap tightly in foil. Place the wrapped pieces of salmon on the same rack in the oven and bake everything at 180°C for 30 minutes. And that's it! Simple, delicious and full of flavor - the perfect idea for a quick, home-cooked dinner!

text: Paranthropus was discovered by paleontologist Robert Broom in 1938, when he identified the species Paranthropus robustus in South Africa. Broom had been searching for fossil evidence to support the existence of hominids close to humans, following the line of research initiated by Raymond Dart, who had described Australopithecus africanus years earlier. The discovery occurred in Kromdraai, South Africa, when a boy named Gert Terblanche found fossil teeth and showed them to Broom. While excavating in the area, the paleontologist discovered a skull that differed from Australopithecus africanus, leading him to classify it as a new species: Paranthropus robustus. text: Have you ever felt like your soul is like a worn fabric? As if, after so much stumbling, so much fighting, so much falling... you could no longer feel at peace again. What happens to the soul when it breaks? What do we do when we don't know how to repair it? Today I want to share a very deep meditation with you. It is not a traditional gospel parable, but it has enormous spiritual power. It is a mystical meditation, attributed to Jesus, collected in the work The God-Man, by María Valtorta. Before continuing, I am going to invite you to subscribe so our videos have greater reach and more people can enjoy them. It does not appear as such in the New Testament, but it is strongly inspired by the real words of Jesus that are in the Gospels, especially in that teaching where he tells us that no one puts a new patch on an old garment, because the new is ruined and the old does not resist. Today we are going to immerse ourselves in this reflection and see what it means when Jesus compares the soul to a cloth that can tear and above all what we can do when we no longer know how to fix it. We take the texts from Man-God, a series of mystical writings by María Valtorta, a 20th century Italian laywoman, who claims to have received visions of the life of Jesus. This reflection is a path to think, feel and let God touch our hearts through a powerful image like the fabric of the soul. Jesus says in this meditation: “I compare the soul to a piece of cloth. When it is unfounded it is new, it has no breaks; only the original stain...¨ That is, when we come into the world, our soul arrives pure, complete, intact. Like a new garment, without seams, tears or stains. But over time, due to wrong decisions, due to wounds we receive and also due to the mistakes we make, that fabric, which is the soul, deteriorates. It gets dirty, it gets stained. It is weakened by vices. It is torn by reckless decisions. It is broken by emotional and spiritual wounds. And not only does it break, but sometimes we try to fix it badly. Like when someone puts any patch, without care, just to cover it up. And what happens is that the original fabric breaks even more. Now what do we do when we are broken? In this meditation Jesus tells us something very important: "Once broken, you should not make a poorly made patch, which would cause other tears... you must do patient and careful work to repair the damage." This tells us about the path of healing, and Jesus tells us: "Do not cover up, Do not mend badly, Do not deceive yourself. If your soul is wounded, do not hide it. Come to me, because I can restore your integrity." And what do we do with pride? Jesus also talks about spiritual pride and says: "The greater the damage in the soul, the more a man tries to hide it with poorly made solutions... and sometimes he does not even ask for help." He who is wounded by diseases, caused in him by unworthy vices, is ashamed of his wounds, and sometimes, he is so completely foolish that he keeps them hidden until the stench reveals them. But then it is too late to remedy it. In this case it refers to broken people, who do not open up to anyone. That they do not ask for forgiveness or that they do not open themselves to God. Jesus says: "The humble is brave. The proud is a coward." The humble one says: "Lord, I am wounded. Heal me." On the other hand, the proud prefers to die with the wound rather than show it. Jesus says: "There are many souls who, out of pride in not having to confess an initial guilt, fall into despair, because they are without God, and saying: "It is too late." And thus, many souls die inside, because they do not have the courage to say: "I am wrong, but I want to change." And Jesus speaks of the wounds and says: "The wounds that a soul has suffered will always be seen. But the soul undertakes its battle and, consequently, receives wounds. The wounds that a soul receives from fighting are not a reason for shame, but for honor. Let's think about the following: a person covered with scars, who fought, that fell, is not despised. On the contrary, she is honest. So, if you fought against your weaknesses, if you went through spiritual battles... your wounds don't make you less, they make you brave. The key is to go to the doctor of the soul, and say: "Lord, here I am. I fought. I fell. But I do not give up. Heal me. Prepare my soul for new battles." What does this meditation want to tell us? That Jesus does not reject us because we are broken. It does not require us to be perfect before approaching. The only thing he asks of us is that we not hide it, that we not deceive ourselves, that we have the humility to say: "I need help." Jesus says: "The mercy of God is stronger than any illness, greater than any error." So, if today we feel that our soul is like an old, torn, stained cloth... Let's not try to cover it. text: ‘The Promise’ - Eugenia: The Crazy Woman Who Killed Again with the Truth. The air in The Promise is no longer the same. Eugenia has returned, and with her, the darkest secrets of the past that the Luján family swore to bury forever. A woman given up for lost in the fog of madness returns with a clear mind and eyes full of blood-curdling knowledge. Is she really cured... or is she just the first pawn in a meticulously planned revenge? Her husband, Captain Lorenzo, watches her with barely concealed fear. For him, her return is not a miracle, but a threat. For Alonso, the Marquis, it is a broken mirror of the past that could reveal his worst crime. And for Curro... it is perhaps the only chance to discover who he really is. The mention of the Count of Ayala, a name that should have remained buried, unleashes a storm: betrayals, covered-up murders, false identities and a conspiracy so well orchestrated that its epicenter could be right in the heart of the family. Who is really Curro's father? Was Eugenia a victim of madness... or of the silence imposed by those who had the most to lose? And what role does the enigmatic Ayala, the man who brought the truth back to La Promesa, play? A truth buried in the garden well. A crime covered by fear and ambition. A woman who was silenced... and now has returned to speak. Prepare for a chapter where nothing is what it seems, and where every look hides an intention, every word a veiled threat. The Promise is no longer a refuge. Now it's a battlefield. Are you ready to know the truth? The air in The Promise had never been so dense, so full of unknowns. Eugenia's arrival had been, as they said, a miracle. A miracle that for Lorenzo, the captain, smelled like a farce; and for others, a threat emerging from the shadows of the past. The woman everyone believed was lost in the fog of madness, Lorenzo's wife, now walked through the halls with a disturbing lucidity, with a calm that was more disarming than any cry of despair. Lorenzo did not hide his suspicion. His grey eyes followed Eugenia's every movement, searching for the crack, the tic, the incoherent word that would prove her supposed recovery was an illusion, a cruel masquerade. "She's faking, I tell you," he muttered to Alonso in the library, a bottle of brandy in his hand. "Her condition was irreversible. The doctors confirmed it. This... this isn't natural. " Alonso, the Marquis, felt like a tightrope walker on a frayed thread. Eugenia's presence made him nervous, rekindling old guilt that he thought was buried. He nodded, trying to calm Lorenzo, but inside, an icy voice whispered: What if he doesn't pretend? What if he remembers? What will happen then? The Luján family gathered in the main room to formally "welcome" Eugenia. There was a mixture of genuine relief at her apparent well-being and an underlying tension that cut through the atmosphere. Eugenia, sitting in an armchair in front of the unlit fireplace – because the heat, she said, was suffocating her – observed everyone with a serene but penetrating gaze. "It has been a long, dark road," she began to relate in a clear voice, with no trace of the confusion of yesteryear. "Sometimes, I felt like I was trapped in a bottomless pit, with my mind covered by a thick fog. But there were moments. Flashes. Moments when a hand held out an anchor to me." Everyone listened, fascinated and apprehensive in equal measure. Who had that hand been? A miracle doctor? An innovative therapy? "That hand." Eugenia continued, making a dramatic pause that seemed to last an eternity. Her eyes rested briefly on Lorenzo, and a glimpse of something indecipherable crossed her gaze. "It was that of the Count of Ayala." The mention of the Count of Ayala fell like a bomb in the room. Alonso cleared his throat. Leocadia, sitting stiffly next to him, paled visibly. Lorenzo let out a sarcastic laugh that echoed in the silence. "Ayala? That charlatan? He 'cured' you? Nonsense!" Eugenia turned her head toward Lorenzo, her expression unchanged. "The Count, Captain, didn't just 'heal' me. He helped me understand. He helped me put the broken fragments of my mind back together. He showed me certain truths I'd been unable to process."Certain truths. The phrase stuck in the minds of Alonso and Leocadia. What truths? How far did Eugenia's knowledge go? Had Ayala told him anything more than his treatment? The question hung in the air, unspoken: What if he already knows everything? Leocadia, unable to bear the tension any longer, excused herself and left. Alonso followed her minutes later, finding her in a secluded hallway, her face covered by her hands. "Leocadia, what's going on?" Alonso asked, more out of instinct than genuine concern for her. "This is a mess, Alonso," Leocadia murmured, taking her hands off her face. "Because Eugenia was always unstable," Leocadia said, but there was an undercurrent of fear in her voice that suggested "unstable" wasn't the right word, but rather "dangerous" or "aware." She returned to her room, now hers by right and by truth. She sat in front of the mirror where the night before she had held that black pin, symbol of lost love, of betrayal, and of rescued memory. She carefully placed it in a red velvet box. She did not cry. Her face was marble. But her eyes… her eyes were more alive than ever. Ayala approached her from behind, silently. “You did well,” he said. Eugenia did not respond. She only offered him a fleeting glance. “And now what will happen to Ricardo?” —Ayala asked in a barely audible voice. He lowered his gaze.—“That… depends on him. It will appear soon. But his return will be even more dangerous than yours. There are those who are not yet ready to face a dead person.”👣 Curro. He wandered through the gardens until dawn. His entire world had shattered. Lorenzo was no longer his father. And his real father… was he alive? A man he didn't know but whose blood beat in his veins? And what place did Eugenia have in all this, now that she was no longer just “the sick mother” but the woman who had remained silent to protect him? Curro stopped by the garden well. He looked inside. Darkness. Silence. Past. And in that instant, he swore something: “I'm going to discover everything.” The whole truth. At all costs. Even if it means destroying what's left of this family. " 👀 Leocadia. She watched from the window of the east wing hallway. Silent. Upright. She didn't speak a single word all morning. But her fingers trembled. She kept letters. Old letters. From Ricardo. From Eugenia. And from someone else. An illegible signature, but with the same seal she now recognized on Ayala's cane. "If Ricardo returns. if Curro accepts it. everything I've done. It won't have served any purpose. " And then, she allowed herself to cry. For the first time in years. 💔 Catalina & Manuel. The secret engagement had vanished in the midst of the family storm. Catalina didn't want to know anything about weddings. Not about Leocadia. Not even about Alonso. "They lied to us all our lives," he said through gritted teeth. Manuel simply nodded. "The only thing I want now. “is to get that plane off the ground,” he murmured, looking at the airplane plans as if they were his salvation. She looked at him harshly, but also with understanding. “Then fly, Manuel. Because here at The Promise we are all falling.”.🕯️ Absolute Closure: The last candle. In the estate’s private chapel, a candle was slowly burning out. In front of it, a hooded figure left an envelope with Curro’s name written by hand. No one saw that person enter. No one saw them leave. Inside the envelope, a document . A will. Not Lorenzo’s. Not Alonso’s. Ricardo de la Mata’s. With a single sentence written in pen: “For you, my son. Before disappearing. I left everything ready.” The flame trembled, and the wax fell like a tear 🕯️ THE END… OR JUST THE BEGINNING? Because when silence falls on The Promise… that's when the true cry of truth begins Ricardo returns. And he doesn't come alone

title: Giro de 180 grados de Antena 3 con la emisión de 'Pasapalabra' este jueves 1 de mayo
text: This Thursday, May 1st, is Labor Day. And since it's a holiday across Spain, television networks have altered much of their regular programming to offer the typical programming of these days with reruns and films. But Antena 3 has surprised with its decision regarding 'Pasapalabra'. .Thus, like every holiday, Antena 3 has opted to replace 'Espejo Público' in the morning with reruns of 'Los Más'. Meanwhile, 'Karlos Arguiñano's Open Kitchen' and 'La ruleta de la suerte' have been broadcast but with reruns like every weekend . And in the afternoon, Antena 3 has also decided to cancel the broadcast of 'Sueños de libertad' and 'Y ahora Sonsoles' to offer instead a double Multicine session with two French films: at 4:00 p.m. "Intocable" and at 6:10 p.m. "Dios mío que te hemos hizo" . However, unlike what has been usual on other holidays, 'Pasapalabra' will not miss its daily appointment with the audience this time. And for some time now the strategy that Antena 3 has followed on holidays has been not to offer new episodes of 'Pasapalabra' and to opt for broadcasting films throughout the afternoon . The comedy, which is produced by Onza and directed by Rodrigo Sopeña, returns with six new episodes full of humor and emotion around a huge traffic jam that will change the lives of its characters. It is an ensemble series in which we can see prominent names from the small screen, such as the collaborator . It is worth remembering that Terelu Campos premiered her first play, Santa Lola, last Saturday in Valladolid. It seems that she has been bitten by the acting bug. In addition to Terelu and Miguel Ángel Revilla, the cast includes Verónica Sánchez, Luis Piedrahita, Luis Zahera, Adriana Torrebejano, Silvia Abril, Goyo Jiménez, Edurne, Paco Tous, Arturo Valls, Carlos Areces, Belinda Washington, Fernando Tejero, Carlos Sobera, Xavier Deltell, Daniel Fez, Josema Yuste, Pepa Rus, Adrián Lastra, Nuria Mencía, Javier Losán and Francisco Reyes . 'El Hormiguero' offers the first images of Miguel Ángel Revilla as an actor Precisely this Wednesday, April 30, two of its actors, Adrián Lastra and Adriana Torrebejano, were supposed to have gone to present the series on 'El Hormiguero' However, due to a family problem, the actress was absent at the last minute, and her place was taken by Josema Yuste In this way, the program presented by Pablo Motos offered exclusively the first images of the second season of 'Atasco' . In them, Miguel Ángel Revilla is seen trapped in the monumental traffic jam, with a driver who is eating a sandwich. He asks him what it is, to which the Cantabrian replies that it is anchovies. Then, the driver tells him that he is allergic, and he begins to feel short of breath. "They have to tell him 'cut' with snipers," joked Pablo Motos, a great friend of the former politician, due to how much he talks, as he demonstrates every time he visits 'El Hormiguero' . In addition, the actors recalled that in its first season, 'Atasco' managed to remain at number 1 on Prime Video for two consecutive weeks. And they have also advanced that in the first minute of the last chapter, there is a "bombshell, surprise." Are they referring to Terelu Campos' cameo? We'll have to wait until May 9th to find out.

title: 13 Mad Engines You Might Not Know About - Part 3
text: You've heard of twin turbos, but what about a train engine that screams like a jet? A rotary that flies and a motorcycle with a handmade V12. And yes, it actually runs. This isn't a list of fast engines. It's a list of madness. Some got banned, some exploded, and some roared so loud they shattered windows. They weren't built to last. They were built to prove something. What engine could run on kerosene, used motor oil, or anything flammable? Which motorcycle outrev Ferraris before they existed? And which engine was silenced just for royalty? Tucker 48, the flat 6 helicopter heart that never took off. There are engines that were designed for power, some for endurance. And then there's one that was designed to fly, but ended up in one of the most ambitious American cars ever built. The air cooled flat 6 engine inside the Tucker 48 wasn't born on the road. It came from the sky. Preston Tucker, the man behind this short-lived dream machine, looked beyond Detroit when designing his revolutionary sedan. What he found was a 5.5 L flat 6 power plant developed for a Bell helicopter producing 166 horsepower without breaking a sweat. And when he dropped it into the rear of his car, history took a sharp turn. Tucker didn't just build a car, he built a statement. a rear-mounted engine, suicide doors, a centered pivoting headlight that turned with the steering wheel, and safety innovations that no other automaker had dared to implement in the 1940s. This car was unlike anything Americans had ever seen. But the flat 6 engine, that's what gave it its soul. Originally designed to be feather light for aviation use, it delivered smooth, torquy power with shockingly little vibration. And it was built tough, intended to run under constant load at altitude, which meant it didn't flinch under road conditions. Unfortunately, the Tucker 48 didn't just challenge engineering norms. It challenged the power structure of the American auto industry. Only 51 cars were made before Tucker was shut down by a mix of political pressure, legal attacks, and industry sabotage. But the engine lived on, a mechanical testament to what could have been. Today, Tucker's flat six-powered sedans sell for millions at auction. And that engine, originally designed to lift a helicopter is now part of automotive legend. From one skybound engine that landed in a car, let's go to an aircraft engine that stayed where it belonged, up in the clouds, but with a twist. Suzuki RG 500 Gamma. The street legal square 42- stroke. Most motorcycles are built with compromise. The Suzuki RG500 Gamma was not. This bike was born on the racetrack and reluctantly handed to the public with a wink and a warning. Underneath its fairings lived a square four two-stroke engine that made no attempt to play nice. 498 cm, 95 horsepower. Power delivery like a chainsaw in a blender. This wasn't just a sport bike. It was a weapon. Each pair of cylinders shared a crankshaft forming a square layout that gave the Gamma razor sharp throttle response and brutal torque delivery. It revved hard. It screamed louder and when it hit the power band, it didn't surge. It detonated. In the hands of a skilled rider, it could humiliate machines twice its size. Before 1932, V8 engines were exclusive, reserved for luxury sedans, race cars, and deep pockets. Then, Henry Ford introduced something that changed everything, the 3.6 L flathead V8. It made 85 horsepower when most engines barely offered half that. More importantly, it was affordable, reliable, and mass-roduced for the everyday driver. The secret was in the side valve design. Instead of placing valves above the pistons, they were mounted beside them, making the engine compact, easier to cast, and cheaper to manufacture. That made power accessible to millions and unleashed a wave of backyard builders and speed junkies. Hot rodders turned junkyard flatheads into stripped down drag monsters. Teenagers in the 1940s and 50s learned to wrench on them. Speed shops built an entire business model around tuning them. This wasn't just an engine. It was the spark that ignited the hot rod revolution. By today's standards, it's heavy, slow, and runs hot. But none of that matters. It's got charm, immediate torque, and a deep, unmistakable American rumble that still shakes the walls of every nostalgia fueled garage from California to Kansas. The Flathead V8 didn't just move cars. It moved a generation. From a working man's dream machine to a cult icon, the Ford Flathead V8 wasn't just a milestone in engine history. That gave the engine a balanced, evenfiring setup with long cylinder bores and massive heads. It had the presence of a V8, but with the raw pull of something built for tanks. title: Cervo Italy: Charming Streets of Cervo - Italy's Timeless Beauty Unfolded
text: Hello friends, welcome to my video I hope you enjoy watching the video and don't forget to like and comment To help grow our channel If possible, subscribe to our channel so you don't miss new videos Cervo - Walk with Me Through the Timeless Beauty of Liguria Welcome to Cervo, a picturesque medieval village perched on the Ligurian coast of northwestern Italy. As we embark on this journey, walk with me through the narrow cobblestone alleys, past pastel-colored houses, and into the heart of a town that has preserved its historical charm for centuries. Cervo's origins trace back to Roman times when it served as a mansio along the Via Julia Augusta, a vital Roman road connecting Liguria to southern France. Its strategic location made it a significant outpost, overseeing maritime routes and facilitating trade. During the Middle Ages, Cervo evolved into a fortified village under the dominion of the Marquises of Clavesana. The Clavesana Castle, constructed in the 13th century, stands as a testament to this era. The castle not only served defensive purposes but also became a symbol of the town's resilience against invasions. In the 17th century, Cervo gained prominence due to its coral fishing industry. Fishermen, known as "Corallini," ventured into the seas near Corsica and Sardinia to harvest precious red coral. The wealth generated from this trade funded the construction of the magnificent Church of San Giovanni Battista, also known as the Church of the Corallini. As we continue our walk, the Church of San Giovanni Battista dominates the skyline with its Baroque façade and intricate stucco work. Built between 1686 and 1778, this church is a masterpiece of Ligurian Baroque architecture. Its concave façade and elevated position offer breathtaking views of the Mediterranean Sea. Adjacent to the church lies the Clavesana Castle, now housing the Ethnographic Museum of Western Liguria. The museum showcases artifacts that narrate the daily lives, traditions, and crafts of the Ligurian people, providing a deeper understanding of the region's rich cultural tapestry. Cervo is not just a relic of the past; it's a living, breathing hub of culture. Since 1964, the town has hosted the International Chamber Music Festival, attracting world-renowned musicians who perform in the enchanting setting of the church square. The natural acoustics of the square, combined with the backdrop of the sea and historic architecture, create an unparalleled musical experience. Literature enthusiasts are drawn to the annual "Cervo ti Strega" event, where finalists of the prestigious Strega Prize present their works, fostering a deep connection between authors and readers in the intimate setting of the village. Walking through Cervo, one can't help but be enticed by the aromas wafting from traditional Ligurian kitchens. The town remains faithful to the Mediterranean diet, with dishes featuring freshly caught seafood, locally produced olive oil, and wines made from indigenous grape varieties like Vermentino. Artisan workshops line the narrow streets, offering handcrafted ceramics, jewelry, and leather goods. These crafts reflect the town's dedication to preserving traditional methods and supporting local artisans. Cervo's location offers a harmonious blend of sea and hills. Olive groves stretch across the terraced landscapes, and the azure waters of the Ligurian Sea provide a serene backdrop. The town's elevation offers panoramic views, making every walk a visual delight. Local legends add a mystical layer to Cervo's rich history. One such tale speaks of a fleet of over a hundred coral fishermen who perished in a storm, leading to the town being dubbed "the land of a hundred widows." Such stories, passed down through generations, infuse the town with a sense of mystery and reverence. As our journey through Cervo concludes, it's evident that this town is more than just a picturesque destination; it's a repository of history, culture, and tradition. From its Roman roots to its Baroque masterpieces, from the melodies of its music festivals to the flavors of its cuisine, Cervo invites visitors to immerse themselves fully. Thank you for joining me on this exploration. May the memories of Cervo's winding alleys, historic landmarks, and vibrant culture linger long after our walk ends.

title: 🩸 5 جرائم أغرب من الخيال… بس حقيقية! 😱
text: There are crimes that are told in novels and crimes that actually happen but no mind believes them. Today, in dark tales with Fawaz, we will dive together into a mysterious world. Five crimes, each one stranger than the other, and all 100% true. Get ready for a group of stories that will make your blood freeze. In 2018, in Berlin, a man named Hans had a fight with his friend in a small apartment. The fight escalated and ended with the death of his friend after he was strangled with a rope. Hans got nervous and decided to deal with the body. He brought a large suitcase, put the body in it with difficulty and called a taxi. The taxi came and the driver helped and carried the suitcase without asking about its strange weight or its smell, which was still light. Hans got out after a while, but he was nervous and busy with his phone and forgot the suitcase and ran out. The driver noticed a strange smell. He opened the suitcase in the garage and was shocked when he found a complete corpse. And wrapped in a sheet, the police came in less than 10 minutes and the cameras easily identified Hans. The strange thing is that when they asked him, he told them he intended to get rid of her, but his mind was confused and he went down and forgot to leave the body in a bag or he didn’t want the taxi to deal with it. Until today, no one knows the answer. The second crime in the state of Ohio in America. A woman named Laura was killed in her house. The door was locked. There was no break-in or theft. Her neighbors canceled the case when she didn’t show up for three days. The police entered and found the body in the bedroom, well covered. The one who killed her knew her. The investigation stopped. There were no fingerprints or witnesses, but there was a cat. Laura’s cat. The investigations focused on her ex-boyfriend, but there was no evidence. The strange thing is that the cat used to get nervous every time he entered the house. The police decided to do something unconventional. They took a hair sample from the cat and it turned out that there were traces of skin on its hair. This is what a man found. The analysis proved that he was her boyfriend. The previous cat without saying a word provided the biggest evidence and the killer was arrested. The third crime: Josh and Rachel went on their honeymoon in the Caribbean Islands. Love, photos, videos. Everything was perfect until the third day. The news broke that Rachel had drowned. Josh said she was swimming and fell into the sea. The police believed him at first, but the autopsy proved that she had died before she touched the water. She had died of suffocation. Suspicion turned to Josh, and after investigations, they discovered a surprise: the hotel cameras had filmed Josh the day before the incident practicing strangling a blanket on the bed, the same way Rachel had suffocated. The motive was her life insurance of $2 million. Josh was sentenced to life imprisonment, and the honeymoon turned into a bloody nightmare. The fourth crime: In a small city in China, Ling discovered that her husband was cheating on her, but her revenge was more horrible than anyone could have imagined. She killed her husband with a dagger and started cutting his body into pieces. Instead of getting rid of him, she decided to cook him. She made soup, rice, and meat dishes and distributed the food to the neighbors. As a social worker, people thanked her, but one day, a neighbor noticed a strange smell in the garbage. He called the police and found human remains. Ling confessed and said he was a traitor and wanted everyone to eat him up like he ate her feelings. A horrible, scary crime, but it happened. The fifth crime in Britain. A thief entered a luxurious villa to rob the door. Luck was with him. He entered easily while he was rummaging through the drawers. The door was forced shut. There was no key, no way out, and the burglar alarm worked, but no one came. He sat inside for four hours, thirsty, hungry, and terrified. He decided to do the stupidest thing possible. He called the police and told them, “I’m locked in a villa and I want someone to get me out.” They asked him, “Who are you?” He told them his real name and found out that he had been reported for theft before. The police came and actually got him out, but to prison. This is a living example of how stupidity is sometimes a crime in itself. Five crimes, each one stranger than the one before it, but they all confirm to us that the truth can be more horrific than any horror movie, if you like. Don't forget to follow Dark Tales with Fawaz because what's coming will scare you more.

title: Hyundai IONIQ 5 2025 | ACR Reviews | Full Review
text: If you think electric cars are all the same, the 2025 Hyundai Ionic 5 is here to prove you wrong. With a bold design, futuristic features, and everyday comfort, this EV isn't just about going green. It's about standing out while doing it. [Music] Let's take a closer look at what makes this car one of the most exciting electric vehicles of the year. Dot. From the front, the 2025 Ioni 5 immediately grabs your attention. The pixel inspired LED headlights give it a unique almost sci-fi look, but in the best way possible. Hyundai has kept the clean lines and sharp angles that made the last model popular, but everything feels more refined now. The wide clamshell hood adds to its bold character, while the thin light bar running across the front creates a sleek, modern edge. It's futuristic without trying too hard, something not many cars get right. Moving to the back, the rear design keeps that pixel white theme going. The tail lights look like they were pulled straight from a video game. But despite the high-tech look, the rear feels balanced and clean, not busy or overdone. The bumper design has been updated slightly, giving it a bit more of a sporty edge. And thanks to the short overhangs and well proportioned tailgate, it manages to stay compact while still looking solid and confident. Now, let's talk wheels. The 2025 Ioni 5 comes with newly designed alloy wheels that perfectly complement the car's sharp styling. The design is geometric and bold, much like the rest of the car. They aren't just nice to look at, they're aerodynamic, too, which helps improve range. Hyundai clearly didn't treat the wheels as an afterthought, and it shows. Step inside and things get even more impressive. The cabin is spacious, minimal, and tech forward without feeling cold. The flat floor and long wheelbase give you more legroom than you'd expect. The dual 12.3 in screens for the gauge cluster and infotainment are bright and easy to use. Hyundai's added more soft touch materials, and even the eco-friendly fabrics feel premium. There's also a sliding center console, customizable ambient lighting, and upgraded seats that offer great comfort even on long drives. Under the hood, or rather under the floor, the 2025 Ionic 5 now offers a bit more punch with a dual motor all-wheel drive option. It can go from 0 to 60 mph in under 5 seconds. The ride is smooth, handling is sharp for an SUV, and it feels planted even on twisty roads. Hyundai also improved the range slightly, now offering up to 310 mi on a single charge, depending on the trim. Charging is still whitening fast with its 800 volt system, up to 80% in about 18 minutes. Now, for the price, the 2025 starts around $43,000. And while that might sound high, it's actually competitive when you consider what you're getting. Between the futuristic design, long list of features, and strong performance, it feels like a good deal in today's EV market. And there may be federal or state tax credits to sweeten the deal, depending on where you live. So, if you're looking for an electric vehicle that's stylish, smart, and seriously fun to drive, the 2025 Hyundai Ionic 5 should be on your list. Don't just take our word for it. Go check it out. Take it for a spin and see why it's turning so many heads. [Music]

title: Natural Camouflage Perk Is Broken | Kingdom Come Deliverance 2
text: As of Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 version 1.2.4, the natural camouflage perk within stealth scale is still not functioning correctly. So, I highly suggest players to avoid using it. On paper, such a move should decrease Henry's visibility if his clothing is soiled. I chose traits I thought would be simple to satisfy. I hate cooking in games, so I didn't choose the food trait, but simple chatting and reading sounded fun and doable. So think about what you'd enjoy doing in-game before you pick your traits. Of course you also need to name your character. Since I desired to become a crime-loving lady of the night, I chose the name Diamond Delight and pimped out my girl with a pretty flashy fit. Your profile is VERY complex, so let me explain each section. The front page lists your family information about your spouse and kids, pets you might have, your political party info, and extracurriculars like basketball league standings, your band, and fight club. If you've been naughty, the top bar shows your crime as well as charisma points from your outfit, prestige points from quests (you can spend these to unlock items), and any debt on your credit card. Your current Pixelian level is in the center, and clicking the Show Details button reveals the various rewards you receive for the first 10 levels. The stats tab shows your traits, which are the three interests you selected at the beginning. Your Talents tab is a summary of the skills you've been improving through your actions. Attributes consist of strength and intelligence, which are each improved through five different activities. You'll need strength for fighting and intelligence for your studies. Education summarizes your college progress as well as homework completion, purchased course credits, and hours you can attend college. The relations tab shows people you've met, and each can be expanded by clicking the info button, and the other tab shows discovered factions and the quests, rewards and perks available for each. If you want to check the days and times that you work or resign from your job, this is in the Career tab, and your dream goals are listed here. Here's your inventory, the housing tab is important because you need to keep paying your rent or you'll suddenly be homeless...this happened to me! At first your map only shows the bus stops, and the other icons populate as you discover the locations. You can use the index at the right to find the building you're looking for and click to add waypoints to guide you along. You can use the bus stops for travel but can later buy a car or a motorcycle. The Pixenville farm map is here as well but won't unlock until level 10 when you can visit. Quests can be viewed and pinned here, and the star button is your creativity hub where unlocked recipes and composed music and books you've written are listed. And finally is the diseases tab. I haven't gotten sick yet, but your ailments will be listed as well as information about contracting each virus. Number three is your dream. After your first day of work, you'll be presented with 10 different dream life options. This gives you goals to complete and is your main story aside from other hobbies you pursue. Currently your dream CANNOT be changed, so this is a crucial decision. I chose mastermind criminal because deviance is an odd fascination of mine, but the goal is frustratingly difficult. I wish I would have chosen supermodel or family person, but the dreams feature gives the game incredible replayability if you're up for the grind. Also, you can have multiple save files if you want different lives. You'll begin the game with subsidized housing in the Clove Apartments. It's small and needs some TLC, but the rent is only about $800 per week. There's a real estate agency you can visit to upgrade your housing, but this is definitely late game territory once you have a high-paying career or sugar daddy. Once you unlock Pixenville, you're given access to a farm house there and all the staple farm tools. It's like having a farming sim game within a city life sim, and you do NOT have to do any farming unless you want. You can also adopt pets for your home. Meet Mr. Krabs. He likes to watch me shower and use the toilet. Nothing weird about that, right? There's a store you can visit to apply for jobs, but the only one available when you begin is being a waiter. You'll work five days per week and need to travel to the restaurant and work within the time window you're given. You'll work five days per week and need to travel to the restaurant and work within the time window you're given. You'll later unlock the job app on your phone for side gigs that will pay about $500 each. If you want a better career, you can go to college and complete 20 classes to graduate and then apply for a new job. Both the waiter and hotel cleaning jobs I tried were interactive careers, requiring a few minutes of simple interaction to complete work and collect a daily paycheck. I also did some hacking once my computer coding skills improved, and I could gain a very small payday when I successfully stole government information or hacked bank accounts. And for science, I bashed a few skulls and looted my fellow Pixelians, but you don't gain much from this, and they will hold grudges against you for beating them up. Number six, you have five basic needs to monitor and satisfy: hunger, energy, toilet, hygiene, and mood. Three of these have easy mini games to complete with simple key presses, and if you wake your character up while they're having a good dream, your mood will be boosted. For your hunger, you do NOT have to cook meals and can just buy pre-made food from shops and cafes. Seven, there are quests and activities everywhere you go. The traits you chose at the start provide constant trait tasks at the bottom left of your screen. Complete these for prestige points and a boost to your mood. You'll also have some story-based quests like stealing government secrets for a faction of hacker girls, infiltrating gangs, playing chess or basketball tryouts, and even participating in political elections (you'll see protesters around the city who are upset about the socioeconomic inequality). But most of the time, it's up to you whether you focus on the quests you are given or want to level up your talent skills. You can go to the movies to boost your mood, watch TV to increase skills, play the stock market, buy books or clothing, get a gym membership and pump some iron, dance at the night club, smash some faces and crack safes, or work on your farming and fishing in Pixenville. Eight, there are over 100 Pixelians to chat with and romance. Talking with people will increase your heart level, and you can call them and arrange to hang out or go on a date. The dates have fun strategic mini game interactions to try and boost your date score. Marriage and kids are also an option, but getting married costs 10,000 dollars and takes a lot of work leveling up the relationship and romance. I landed myself a doctor who will hopefully grant me access to his prescription pad and bank account. Mama needs her Xanax and Botox! Number nine, To Pixelia performed great. There aren't any video settings nor an option to run on ultrawide monitors, but the movement was smooth and didn't even ramp up my PC fans. It does play well on Steam Deck too, though controller gameplay is a little awkward with the right thumbstick acting like a cursor. And the 15 dollar price tag completely surprised me. There's no true END to the game, and although it no doubt will have updates to fix some things, the amount of gameplay per dollar makes this an excellent value. I paid double this price when I backed it on Kickstarter. And number 10, I had two main frustrations that may or may not matter to you: lack of guidance and considerable grind. I can't stress enough that THIS GAME NEEDS A WIKI! I was constantly searching their Discord and Steam Forum to find out how to rotate furniture, how to heal my health, where to get food, where to find clothing I bought, and how to complete quests. The biggest issue for me was my dream of becoming a criminal being blocked by not knowing how to pick locks and not finding the people I needed to commit crimes against since the quests did not provide waypoints. The guidance could use some polish, and I think some functionality just isn't in the game yet but hopefully will be soon. The other potential frustration is slow progression. For example, to increase strength, there are mini games for each weight machine, but as you level up, it will physically hurt your fingers to spam and spam and spam the keys to accomplish one rep on the machine, and you have to do this for five different machines. title: Man who fell from 21-foot Clemente Wall at PNC Park during Pirates game in critical condition
text: Scary moment for everyone inside PNC Park as a man fell over the outfield wall onto the playing field. Uh and Pittsburgh public safety says that he's now in critical condition at the hospital. Now last night during the Pirates Cubs game, the man fell from the right field bleachers above the 21 ft Clemente wall and landed on the warning track. Trainers, police, and EMS responded immediately to tend to the fan who they placed on a stretcher and carded off the field. He fell moments after Andrew McCutchen hit an RBI double in the bottom of the seventh inning to put the Pirates up four to three. Those in attendance watched it all unfold. You did see some of the players take a knee. Um, everyone in the outfield was kind of talking about what happened cuz being there, you heard some rumblings of like his friend hopped down on the field and but no one knew their exact story. We were just trying to figure it out. A fan jumped from a lower section of the outfield wall to help the person who fell. It's unknown if that person was a family member, friend, or a bystander. The game was delayed for about 10 minutes before play resumed in the bottom of the seventh inning. The Pirates beat the Cubs 4 to3. After the game, the team manager said this was an extremely unfortunate incident, calling that an understatement. And McCutchen also posted on X formerly known as Twitter saying, "Can't help but think about that guy, his family and friends. Let us think about his loved ones and hug our families a little tighter tonight. I hope he pulls through." The incident remains under investigation. At this time, it's unclear whether drugs or alcohol played any factors. For now, reporting from PNC Park, Lauren Linder, CBS News, Pittsburgh.

title: Indie Games are TAKING OVER 2025!
text: What’s going on squad? I hope you’re all doing well. I am making another more focused video which should be out soon, but I thought based on the good response of my last video, and the fact it was a lot of fun to make, I’d double down and give you guys 10 more really promising upcoming 2025 indie games. I gotta shout out you guys for putting me onto some cool stuff in the comments of the last video, a few of which are in this video! A lot of what’s going on in the indie game scene recently is really inspiring and cool. Some of our generation’s most interesting artists are working in this medium, I really love that making games is now fairly accessible, and these passion projects can come into fruition so often. It’s an antidote to the hyper-commercialized mainstream live-service stuff to see such impressive, smaller scaled games being made so frequently, often which aim to experiment a little bit more, or even just make really honest heartfelt homages to other older games. Not only that, but I’ve had a lot of fun just scouring the market for what’s on offer and finding the weirder, more off the radar stuff that could end up becoming a cult classic or even possibly crossing over into the mainstream. I’m sure it’s still decent, but the fact that the ‘game of the moment’ is a slightly spruced up version of a game from 2006 is not the best reflection for the levels of creativity that is present in the video game landscape. Anyways, If you saw the last video, you know the deal. I’ll run through ten games and tell you why each of them has promise and what I enjoyed about its demo. All of these have a demo available live on steam, so if you want to give any of them a spin then they’re just a few mouse clicks away. Let’s get to it! We’ll start things off with something that, slight hyperbole here, could legit become one of my favourite games of all-time. It’s passing the sleepycore vibe check so hard that it’s kinda scary. Unbeatable is a rhythm slash visual novel RPG sort of game, and gotta be real with you all, THIS GAME HIT ME LIKE CRACK BRO. I need another hit now, I don’t care if this game ruins my life, I’ll be begging on the streets for more. I’ll be committing crimes to get my Unbeatable fix. This is just so crazy cool. A beautiful art style featuring a sort of washed out, CRT fuzziness overtop the slick 2D animated characters and simple, yet striking 3D environments. This is really high quality stuff. It has me recalling a bunch of stuff I really like, like Scott Pilgrim, FLCL, Persona 4 and 5. These all came to mind while I was playing this. Those are all things that release dopamine into my brain just thinking about them, so forgive me for the disgusting fanboy hype here. Its hazy atmosphere and lighting was amazing, really struck a chord with me for sure. Surreal dream sequences, with some striking direction for the simple text box dialogue scenes. Seems like the story is quite detailed with a big focus on the exploration and character development just as much as there are the rhythm game sections. I really enjoyed these environments, they were bursting with character and the art style make simple environments still look quite impressively lit. These rhythm game sections are pretty fun too, just uses two buttons but, while I’m not the best judge cos I suck at these sort of games, it seemed like it was challenging enough and filled with variety. It’s got an original soundtrack too, featuring a bunch of artists and different remixes. Definitely fits the vibe of the game, and I was enjoying the indie rock and electronic leaning tracks in particular. I was glad that it wasn’t a game soundtracked by, like, electro-swing, I guess. On the whole, this was just so unbelievably cool, the sort of game I already know I’ll be downloading day 1 to give it a spin because the amount of love put into it seems to be unbelievable, and it’s quite distinct in its visual novel meets rhythm game premise as well. Really seems a cut above what you’d expect from an indie studio in a lot of ways. Now let’s sidestep to a more traditional rhythm game. This is HYPERBEAT, which has an intriguing lo-fi aesthetic paired with banging electronic music. Makes me think of Rez for the PS2 immediately, though it plays fairly different. You navigate your knight down this tube and hit targets along the way which are in time with the beat, some of which also require a specific button press. I got my ass kicked on the harder levels on offer in this demo but did find it a lot of fun. It’s a pretty challenging game, but when you’re in the zone and doing well, you start to feel like a god. I was enjoying the mysterious vibes in the game’s presentation too, where you’re in this strange church-like area and knights with uncanny robot voices will speak some cryptic wisdom to you. Consider me intrigued by this aesthetic because it’s not something I’d naturally associate with the kind of music on offer here, but it kinda works for me. There’s this weird esoteric feel to the game. Not only that, but I was getting along well with the bouncy soundtrack and the visuals ended up quite striking, it’s a great example of how you can create a great look for a game within limitations. It’s supporting steam workshop too so I assume I can load up the game with custom tracks. So get me in some 2012 era Skrillex, and I’m pretty much sorted. Another very stylish game is Mindwave. This is essentially Warioware, but with a visual novel element to pad it out.

I used to play Warioware Twisted on an emulator on my jailbroke ipod touch back in the day too, cos the actual game never came out in Europe. Eurobros getting shafted once again… Another L for the pile. But what makes Mindwave more than a pastiche is such strong visual style, with this scibbly pixel art and sick character designs that really leave an impression. The writing seems sharp, which works well to break-up the microgames and act as an edgier foil to the wackiness of the gameplay. It seems really promising for sure. This is dripping with style front to back and even the microgames are accompanied by a vocal pop song, it’s really something that got me smiling over the course of a short demo. Sure it’s derivative of Warioware, but since none of the recent Warioware’s have ever really seemed to appeal to me, I’m probably more down for this pastiche than anything Nintendo might pull off. Especially if the quality shown in this demo is consistent for a bunch more levels. I don’t think I’m ever defeating the 3D platformer fanboy allegations. I swear I like other games too man. But hey, here’s another 3D platformer that’s cool as hell. This is 500 Calibur Contractz, actually it’s one of the strangest games I’ve played in a while. Immediately I was intrigued by its ‘00s aesthetic. This is going so hard into like, early ‘00s internet forums, but also taps into more current dystopian anti-corporate feelings too. This character looks like that deviantart mascot and Sephiroph had an extra edgy love child. I guess the premise is that various employees of the most soulcrushing corporations crowdfund for a hitman to kill the CEO of their company, and Edgy McEdgelord takes the call. This is like a 3D Mario game if Mario was THIS Luigi’s brother instead. A pitch of “what if Mario 64 had a sniper rifle” is actually pretty accurate. It’s a movement platformer that feels quite different to most stuff I’ve played, you use the sniper to gain aerial momentum and launch yourself across the level. Check this out, they’re throwing me a party to celebrate me killing their boss :) and hey they’re using wordart just like I would in primary school to make the most insane powerpoints of all-time. ‘00s kids… Our time is now. This is something I’m actually all the way down for in terms of its aesthetic. Its demo was a lot of fun to play, even though the actual level on offer doesn’t have a massive amount to do in it and the actual key goal of the assassination felt somewhat anticlimactic. But it’s built in such a way that rewards repeat plays, and it definitely feels really satisfying once you get to grips with platforming with a sniper rifle and keeping your momentum up. There’s a tips n tricks video soundtracked by this insanely cool ‘00s nu-metal throwback song by Shimaigami too. Had me cracking up with the Windows Movie Maker transitions and chirpy text slides. Feels like it washed right up from 2008 era YouTube. I can’t think of any game that leans so hard into this post-y2k type aesthetic. Really seems like this music theme could pair well with the character switching. It’s like you’re conducting a symphony of violence. I definitely like it’s cel-shaded, Soul Eater inspired art style and the anime style character’s have a similar sort banter as the gang in Persona 5 as well. Seems like these devs really have an affinity for the games they're influenced by. I found this very satisfying to play, its combat seemed up right up my alley and the platforming aspects, while simple, were fun changes of pace to bridge the battle sequences together. The demo only has two out of the four characters to play as, but both play really nice and the ability to so smoothly switch between the gang is much appreciated and seems like it will lead to hugely satisfying gameplay if you’re to invest time to get good at it. This is Aurascope, a 2D platformer that is structured like a 3D mario game and crossed with a Metroidvania. So think like: Mario 64, Sunshine or Galaxy meets something like Shantae or Guacamelee… This means it’s one where instead of the goal being get to the end of the level, point a to point b type stuff, you’ve got more open levels that have multiple objectives that you’ll return to. I don’t think I’ve seen any 2D platformers take the 3D Mario formula, so this was quite a bit of fun to see pulled off so well as in Aurascope. There’s a good amount of variety to the objectives and tasks, it’s got fun collectathon elements that reward exploration as well. It dips its toes into Metroidvania type of structure as well and has you doing these little side quests in the hub world too. There’s even a split-screen vs. mode which is something extra that seems pretty cool. This controls very nicely, the characters have got a sick diving jump move that definitely feels satisfying to use. This pixel art is pretty high quality too, and obviously you can see it’s very colourful, bright and eye-catching. Last time I talked about the Sonic fan game to original title pipeline, and something similar is that this game’s solo dev actually started off making Mario fan games, and is now making his own original title. Aurascope was a lot of fun and the demo available is surprisingly meaty, with lots to do, and you really get a good feel for what the full game will be like,. It’s something I’m definitely very interested in. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater is back this year with remakes of the third and fourth games in the series, and I’m sure we’ll get Underground and American Wasteland remakes too, because that’s our lives now. Everything will be remade and then probably remade again in 15 years. I can just play the originals on dolphin whenever, so I’m more inclined to check out Olliefrog Toad Skater instead. It’s obviously quite derivative of the Tony Hawk’s games from the late ‘90s and early ‘00s. But this feels really tight to play and I adore the simple, cutesy, pastel art style. You can get your frog looking drippy with a character creator and then go shred the spot. Sure, Tony Hawk’s might have Bam Margera and all these brand crossovers. But Olliefrog lets you play as a moustache frog and wear Gurren Lagann sunglasses, so who’s really winning? This seems pretty promising, with pick up and play arcadey level design as well as a more in-depth career mode on offer too. Its soundtrack choices were on point, with pop-punk & metalcore adjacent stuff as well as more varied electronic tracks too. Here we have My Familiar, which is a new RPG that’s shaping up to be very interesting. This drew me in immediately with such a strong pixel art aesthetic. I particularly like the sort of twilight, purply tint to the game. Its setting of “Wish City” is interesting too because it’s so grimy and run down. It has a similar sort of vibe as the original Final Fantasy VII when you’re exploring the Midgar slums. One of my formative gaming moments was playing this section of FFVII so anything that throws back to that feeling has me getting big dopamine hits man. It’s full of questionable, seedy characters and even through the pixel art you can tell this place stinks. It’s a really rich setting, and I was hooked and reeled right in by it. There’s some sort of real world and fantasy world dichotomy in the plot as well, which is intriguing. I thought the writing was pretty sharp, it’s cool to have a game where your party members aren’t going to be typical RPG archetypes. This guy who joins is a raging alcoholic, like this dude’s just down horrendous. As for its battle system, it’s pretty typical turn based stuff but with timing based systems to boost your attack power. It’s not blowing me away as much as the setting and vibe, but it more than does the job for me. I do really like these animations and backgrounds, like this beachy sunset background is really cool for sure. It’s got such a jazzy soundtrack too, which fits so, so well. All the art was really nice, the world-building was strong, and I liked the grimy tone a whole lot too. My Familiar definitely seems like a potential cult classic lying in wait to be discovered. Another RPG that’s caught my eye is Pillory. A dazzling black & white title that leans in heavy on a weird, surreal tone. title: From Noob to Pro: Expedition 33 Tips That Break the Game!
text: What's up everybody, I want to give you some tips and tricks to boost your gameplay in Expedition 33. Thank you for joining me for this video, my name is Wak4863, but you can call me Wak. Starting right off on your way to the Gomage you want to look for Richard. He's pretty easy to spot in his red outfit, chat with him and he is going to give you a unique quest item, Richard's Sons Uniform. Not too far away from Richard, you're going to find another person to chat with. This is Eloise, you want to talk with her so you can go through a tutorial on using some of Gustav's skills and get a reward for completing that. The key to getting this done is to reach overcharge on your arm and then you're going to use Gustav's skill overcharge in order to defeat the balloon with a single strike. And your reward for doing this is a color of lumin. You're also going to want to stop at the Painter in order to go through another tutorial and get some good rewards. title: You Should Try: White Knuckle – A Ruthlessly Addictive Speed-Climbing Roguelite
text: Desperately climbing away from an all-consuming ooze doesn’t sound like a jolly good time, yet somehow, White Knuckle makes it ruthlessly addictive. Thanks to extremely tight controls, a slew of challenging-but-fair obstacle courses, and a dystopian world so bizarre that I *need* to know more about it, White Knuckle has completely devoured my past few days. At its core, White Knuckle is an astonishingly simple game. You can jump, you can sprint, and you can grab onto things with either hand in order to climb. If you're feeling particularly spicy, you can even latch onto ledges with both hands to hoist yourself up faster. What you can't do is hold on forever as your titular white knuckles will quickly start turning bright red, thus warning you that your stamina is running out and that your grip is about to fail. To avoid a grizzly fall you'll need to either find a perch to rest up on, or if safe haven is nowhere to be found, alternate between each hand to buy yourself just enough time to crawl to safety. If you find yourself in a situation where progress looks impossible - or if you spot a potential shortcut - you can also use one of your limited items to create new handholds on the fly. And considering how this usually involves hurling a piece of rusty rebar straight through thick, industrial concrete, I wouldn’t be even slightly surprised if it turns out that the player character is actually just Popeye. It would certainly explain how he replenishes his supernatural strength by shotgunning cans of what I can only assume is concentrated spinach. And that's pretty much it as far as the mechanics are concerned. Yet despite how simple it all is, there is a lot of depth, complexity and skill expression to be found here. And more importantly, a lot of fun as well! Once you get into the right rhythm there's just something mesmerizing about swinging from handhold to handhold, making snap decisions on when to expend stamina jumping and when to take it slow, or just throwing caution to the wind to take a supremely risky shortcut purely for the hell of it! But it's when you get put under pressure that White Knuckle, or Sweaty Palm as it really should've been called, becomes truly transcendent. When there's danger all around you and you're desperately trying to survive the onslaught just so you can get a tiny bit further than you've ever been, that's when the magic happens. In these moments I find that all rational thought evaporates from my brain. I seem to enter a sort of fugue state where the only things that exist are the next few handholds and the obstacles preventing me to reach them. Everything else just kind of fades away until I reach a safe space where I can finally relax, take a deep breath and savor my victory - but only for a brief moment as there's always more to climb! It's not just the movement mechanics — the level design is also rock solid despite being somewhat procedurally generated on account of White Knuckle being a roguelite. The way it works is that each section you approach draws from a pool of hand-crafted 'levels' with a couple of elements randomly added or removed in order to make them more replayable. Sometimes this means you'll have to completely change your strategy as there's a nasty enemy in an unexpected place; sometimes a pathway you're used to might become more treacherous, and sometimes it might be as simple as you getting a few extra items to incentivize you to take the faster, riskier routes. The downside of this approach is that you'll eventually see most of the variations, especially in the first two zones as you'll be frequently climbing through them to get back to the much more difficult later stages of the game. The upside is that all of the areas are actually designed and tested by human beings which means that all of them, and I really do mean all of them, have a solid flow and work well with White Knuckle's mechanics. So as far as I'm concerned, these light roguelite elements are implemented really well - they add just enough spice to keep each level fresh, but without actually detracting from its quality. And quality is exactly what they are, as each individual chunk seems purpose-built around celebrating a certain mechanic or obstacle type, which makes each one feel unique even though they're all industrial nightmares. For example, you can ask any White Knuckle player what they think about the ventilator room with the button... and chances are they'll instantly be able to draw a rough layout from memory. The individual levels really do stick out, and I think a big reason for that is that they're all at the center of at least one story of glorious triumph or bitter failure. Another aspect of the level design that I greatly appreciate is how clear and obvious the pathways are. Unless the room you're in is intentionally cryptic to get you to make your own routes with items or by using the environment, each area in White Knuckle does a pretty good job of guiding your view towards the next series of obstacles you need to conquer - all the way to the very top. This might not sound like a big deal now, but when you're frantically climbing away from the grey sludge of doom devouring everything below you, knowing where to go - and how to get there quickly - becomes very important, very fast. Oh and speaking of the sludge, that... uhh, thing, essentially serves as a timer to encourage you to push forward and utilize momentum to your advantage over simply playing it slow and safe. It's terrifying when it's right behind you, and I've messed up plenty of times because I panicked in its presence, but as far as world-ending eldritch horrors go

title: You Should Try: White Knuckle – A Ruthlessly Addictive Speed-Climbing Roguelite
text: think a big reason for that is that they're all at the center of at least one story of glorious triumph or bitter failure. Another aspect of the level design that I greatly appreciate is how clear and obvious the pathways are. Unless the room you're in is intentionally cryptic to get you to make your own routes with items or by using the environment, each area in White Knuckle does a pretty good job of guiding your view towards the next series of obstacles you need to conquer - all the way to the very top. This might not sound like a big deal now, but when you're frantically climbing away from the grey sludge of doom devouring everything below you, knowing where to go - and how to get there quickly - becomes very important, very fast. Oh and speaking of the sludge, that... uhh, thing, essentially serves as a timer to encourage you to push forward and utilize momentum to your advantage over simply playing it slow and safe. It's terrifying when it's right behind you, and I've messed up plenty of times because I panicked in its presence, but as far as world-ending eldritch horrors go it's actually quite alright. You're never under *that* much pressure, so once you've gotten accustomed to the movement mechanics you'll only ever have to deal with it when you screw up *really* badly, which is still preferable to simply getting annihilated and sent back to the start menu. That said, you're still going to get quite familiar with the start menu. While White Knuckle is generally extremely fair with its challenges, it does not shy away from presenting you with some truly devious gauntlets. I'd like to think I'm fairly experienced with its mechanics at this point, and even still I find myself dying in the second or third zone because it's so easy to slip up, panic instead of salvaging the situation, and then dunk yourself directly into the carnivorous sludge. However, while it may be punishing to the careless, White Knuckle is not cruel. The challenge ramps up relatively slowly, and all of the crazy trials you'll have to best later have very clear roots in the fairly easy levels at the very start. So just by trying and failing you'll put in a decent amount of time into practicing the basics. So while it might seem annoying having to restart every time you kick the bucket, the process of learning how to speedrun those first few sections is exactly what will make you better at tackling the wildest hazards White Knuckle can throw at you. There's only one exception to all of this, and it's essentially my only real complaint with White Knuckle. When you're climbing and you jump you'll expend a fair bit of stamina in order to leap upwards as you would expect. But when you do that near an incline there's a chance you can just launch yourself backwards which is almost guaranteed to be a run-ender. Whether this is just a mechanic I don't understand or a bug, I have no idea, but even though I've learned how to work around it I still don't like how jarring and unnatural it feels, especially when the rest of the game is so buttery smooth. While it's easy to overlook it since you'll be hard-focused on trying not to lose your grip while climbing, White Knuckle has a really surreal and surprisingly compelling world. The visuals, the audio, the screen effects - all of it gives off this grimy, dirty, dystopian atmosphere of true hopelessness. Nothing *ever* feels right. Even when you reach areas that have been untouched by whatever calamity has befallen the facility it still doesn't feel comfortable, or like a place where you can rest. Instead, it feels more like a facade - something hastily slapped over a gaping wound in the universe in the hopes that not looking at it will make the problem go away. The story is similarly incomprehensible and mostly comes from environmental clues and the occasional announcement message, but there's enough interesting elements to it that I'm slobbering to learn more. It's obvious that some kind of experiment went wrong and now there's an apocalyptic sludge rising from below, but what in the world are those ungodly noises that sometimes emanate from above us? Is the sludge the reason the facility is collapsing or has the collapse simply enabled it to escape? Is the beast above us a completely unrelated experiment that also went haywire? Are we one of the experiments? I have no idea, but like I said at the very beginning, I *need* to learn more about this nightmare that White Knuckle calls reality. The final, and perhaps most important note, is that White Knuckle has only just released into Early Access. So while it already has an immense amount of content - and polished content at that - it's not even close to being finished. And in an era where Early Access games can release straight up broken, that really is quite impressive. So if everything I've shown you thus far has piqued your curiosity, I would heartily recommend you give White Knuckle's demo a try. It spans the game's first three 'sections' and offers way more gameplay than you would expect, so it should give you a pretty good idea of what the full version is like. Enjoy, and I hope you end up losing yourself in it just like I have! Thank you for watching, and if you enjoyed this, or even if you didn't, please do let me know. Thank you for sticking to the end, and I hope you have a lovely day. Bye, bye!
