title: Jupiter - Il Destino dell'Universo delle sorelle Wachowski | JM'S GUILTY PLEASURE Ep. 6
text: Hi guys, welcome back to Wikos! I'm John Mira and today we continue with the Guilty Pleasure column, the column where I recommend bad movies, but they can entertain. And today's movie is Jupiter original title Jupiter Ascending from 2015. The directors of this film are only the Wachowski sisters. I won't dwell on who they are, but they made a movie called The Matrix in 1999. That is, they revolutionized cinema. But unfortunately they had ups and downs and this film is a low. Why Jupiter is the easiest work written by the Wachowski sisters - It really is their most basic film! I point this out because in 2012 they directed and wrote Cloud Atlas, a really complicated work, and so when viewers read 'from the directors of The Matrix and Cloud Atlas' they expect a work that is perhaps a little complicated, where the brain works a lot. Instead, Jupiter is a very simple work, the total opposite! In this film we find a girl who works in a cleaning company, and discovers that she is an intergalactic princess! And the girl with the help of a wolf warrior will have to save the earth from an ancient threat. The film went very badly. The viewers, in my opinion, expected something else. Yes, the film is spectacular at times and entertains quite well. But it's really very, very linear. Because the screenwriters seem to have gone by subtraction from the past. They said 'let's do a basic and simple thing, let's see how it goes.' A kind of response to the so-called young adults of that period. We focus less on substance and also a little more on feelings. Not that this concept of cinema is wrong - a film in simplicity can also excite, but unfortunately the two people behind the camera had too heavy a baggage. But in fact I don't consider this film a wrong work, but the public wanted more. And the film is a lot of fun. In the first half hour we get to know various characters and especially the first 10 minutes are beautiful: we get to know the parents of the protagonist in an almost surreal atmosphere. And that part, in my opinion, is narrated very well. And the film is part of those categories where the first half has many pleasant things and lays many foundations. But the last part, the whole second half, this thing fades away. In the first part you laugh, there are spectacular scenes, and in the third act the film becomes really linear and sometimes caciarone. And it seems that the film is also too short: a lot of stuff is put in the cauldron, and the film is as if it were cut quickly in the editing room at some point. And the viewer, unfortunately, is left with a bitter taste in his mouth. It also seems that the work had budget problems, that is, it seems that they had a certain type of sum, but during filming this nest egg has always become less. And so they had to cut. And the film is quite expensive: visual effects, sets, costumes - all well made. But as mentioned, the third act takes the breath away from the opera - noise, speed in editing, all very very fast. It's pretty much the same problem we saw in The Mummy with Tom Cruise. The film is a kind of work and perhaps it was supposed to be the beginning of a new saga. And it is told with fairytale tones in certain moments: the princess, the warrior who has to help the threat, and then here too it seems that the film has become a self-contained work. Maybe they wanted to tell other adventures with Mila Kunis and Channing Tatum. As for the cast, I point out that she doesn't always work very well - at times she seems out of the way; Tatum is perfect. Eddie Redmayne as the villain in over acting. He is also a character who is not very well written. And an ever-great Sean Bean - I won't tell you if he dies in the movie or not. The soundtrack by Michael Giacchino is very good. But as mentioned, more had to be given to the viewer. We wanted more. Remember to follow Wiko on all social networks: X, Facebook, YouTube, Instagram. Like the video, share it, and we'll see you at the next episode of Guilty Pleasure, bye!

Excitement Builds Around "玫瑰丛生" (Roses in Bloom) as Multiple Title Changes Spark Heated Debate The upcoming drama 玫瑰丛生 (Roses in Bloom), starring 王子文 (Wang Ziwen) and 刘宇宁 (Liu Yuning), is generating immense buzz as it gears up for its May premiere. Based on the highly rated Douban manga 蝉女 (The Cicada Woman), which boasts an impressive 8.8 rating, this show is a blend of romantic tension, emotional drama, and a distinctive aesthetic. However, the drama has also become a talking point due to its several title changes, which have sparked much discussion and controversy among fans and viewers alike. A Dramatic Transformation: From Manga to Screen 玫瑰丛生 is adapted from 蝉女, a popular and highly acclaimed manga that has garnered a strong following for its compelling narrative and intriguing characters. The manga follows the emotional complexities of its protagonist, and the drama seeks to capture that essence by delving deep into themes of loyalty, deception, and the fragility of human relationships. At the heart of the drama is 王子文’s portrayal of 廖兮 (Liao Xi), a "relationship expert" whose job is to measure the loyalty of men—a rather fascinating, yet troubling concept that sets the stage for an intense love triangle. Liu Yuning and 高伟光 (Gao Weiguang) join Wang Ziwen in this emotional rollercoaster, as their characters become entangled in a complex love triangle. This scenario has sparked comparisons to the classic trope of the "thumbelina and giant" combination, where two unlikely figures find themselves in an almost impossible relationship dynamic. Fans are eagerly awaiting to see how this relationship unfolds, especially given the immense chemistry that the cast is expected to bring to the screen. Aesthetic and Real-World Ties: The Black, White, and Red Aesthetic One of the standout features of 玫瑰丛生 is its striking visual aesthetic. The show promises to stay true to the manga’s core themes, especially the prominent use of black, white, and red tones, which symbolize the juxtaposition of love, betrayal, and passion. These colors aren’t just a stylistic choice—they encapsulate the emotional turmoil and moral ambiguity that the characters experience. This careful attention to detail in the visual department is another reason why fans have high hopes for the show’s success. Furthermore, the series isn’t just a fictional tale of romance—it is designed to reflect real-world cases of emotional manipulation and deceit. With elements taken from actual news stories, 玫瑰丛生 will likely feel more grounded and relatable to audiences who are familiar with these types of issues. The drama's incorporation of real-life cases adds a layer of intensity, suggesting that viewers will be forced to confront uncomfortable truths about relationships and trust. As the tagline goes, this is not just a drama; it’s a mirror that reveals the darkest truths about love and loyalty.

title: How to Add Commentary in eFootball 2025?
text: Hello everyone, welcome back to our channel. In today’s video, I am going to show you how to add commentary in eFootball. So let’s get started! First of all, open the eFootball app and wait for it to fully load. Once you’re on the home screen, tap on the "Extras" tab found at the top right corner of the screen. From there, tap on “Game Settings.” Inside the settings menu, select "Download Data." Here, you will find "Commentary Language." Tap on it, and you’ll see a list of available commentary languages. Choose your preferred language and then hit the download button. The download might take a few minutes depending on your internet speed. Once it’s finished, the commentary will automatically be activated in your matches. If you ever want to switch languages or remove commentary, just return to the same settings and make your changes. title: Cold Fusion Idea Makes Comeback
text: There's a type of cold fusion that actually works and has been experimentally verified for decades. It's called muon catalyzed fusion. And yes, there are actually people working on it. Last month, researchers demonstrated a new way to produce muons using lasers, potentially solving one of the biggest practical challenges. And a startup called Accelerant Fusion is raising money to save the world with mun catalyzed fusion. Just how crazy is this? Let's have a look. The biggest problem with nuclear fusion is that atomic nuclei are all positively charged. So they repel each other. You need to overcome this electric repulsion first until the strong nuclear force sets in. If the nuclei have electrons around them, this shields the charge of the nucleus up to some distance. But the electron orbits are so far away from the nucleus that this shielding doesn't allow you to get the nuclei close enough. Enter muons. Muons are elementary particles similar to electrons but about 200 times heavier. And because muons are so much heavier, their energy orbitals around atomic nuclei are much smaller. This means if you replace the electron around a hydrogen atom with a muon, you can bring the nuclei closer together without the electric repulsion getting in the way and that much increases the fusion probability even at room temperature. The mon acts as a catalyst. Hence, it's called immune catalyzed fusion. This was theoretically predicted already in the 1940s and first experimentally confirmed in the 1950s. So not like this is a new idea. But if this works, why aren't we powering the world with mun catalyzed fusion already? As you probably guessed, there are a few problems. The first problem is that mons are unstable. They can only catalyze so many fusions until they decay. This wouldn't be such a big issue if it wasn't for the second problem, which is that in about 1% of fusion reactions between dutyium and tritium, the muon gets stuck to the helium nucleus and then it can't catalyze any more fusions. This means that the number of available muons decreases. Typically, a muon only manages to catalyze about 100 fusion reactions. The observed record was 150 and that dates back to the 1980s when people still had time for this kind of thing. That the immune get stuck also wouldn't be such a big issue if it wasn't for the third problem. Muon production is currently done with particle accelerators and those aren't known for being energy efficient. So you need to put in vastly more energy than you get out of the fusion. But that was the status in the 1980s and technology has come a long way since. Indeed, the startup Acceleron Fusion now wants to bring MUN catalyzed fusion to the market. In December, they raised $24 million to get it done with a proton accelerator. They shoot the protons into a target, which creates pions that then decay into muons. To make their technology produce net energy, they need to make the proton acceleration as efficient as possible. And they also have a plan to avoid that the mons get stuck so quickly on the helium by putting the fuel under pressure, some thousand times atmospheric pressure. I'm somewhat skeptical that the proton accelerator will ever become energy efficient, but maybe the following can help. In March, researchers from the UK and Romania demonstrated a new way to produce muons. They do it with laser wakefield acceleration. Yes, that's the same technology that could shrink accelerators back down to something that doesn't take billions of dollars. International agreements and the Geological Survey. Laser Wakefield acceleration works by shooting a laser pulse into a gas, typically hydrogen. The laser deposits energy into the gas which blasts electrons away leaving behind a region of rapidly moving positive charge. This pulls in electrons from behind so it accelerates them. This technology can produce electron energies in the range of some giga electron volts over just a few cm. In comparison, the LHC has a pre-acelerator that speeds protons up to similar energy, but that's more than 100 m in circumference. Wakefield acceleration isn't yet good enough to actually build bigger particle colliders, but producing mons. Now, that's a different thing. So in this new study, the researchers used laser wakefield acceleration to create GV electrons, dump those into a lead target, and that produced about 10,000 m per shot. Now, to be fair, they used a petawatt laser, which is still some 20 m long or so. So if you want to call that a tabletop experiment, you'd need a very long table. And lasers aren't known for being energy efficient either. But that's still a remarkable achievement which puts forward an entirely new avenue for muon production. Muon catalyzed fusion isn't going to power our homes anytime soon. But if they can get it to work, then particle physicists can brag that their accelerators were good for something after all. title: The Best Foods to Burn Belly Fat (That Actually Work)
text: If you're looking to burn fat, it's time to ditch the fat diets and start making smarter food choices. The key to fat loss isn't starving yourself. It's about fueling your body with the right foods that actively help you burn fat and boost your metabolism. Let's dive into some of the best fat burning foods you should be eating more of. First up, protein. Protein is essential for fat loss and it should be the foundation of your meals. Things like lean chicken, turkey, fish, and eggs are loaded with protein which helps build muscle. Why is muscle important because muscle burns more calories even when you're at rest? So the more muscle you have, the more fat your body can burn throughout the day. Protein also keeps you feeling full longer which can help curb those hunger cravings that lead to overeating. Next let's talk about fiber-rich vegetables. Fibers like spinach, kale, broccoli, and cauliflower are not only packed with nutrients but they're also high in fiber which is essential for fat loss. Fiber helps keep you feeling satisfied longer so you're less likely to reach for unhealthy snacks. Plus fiber helps regulate blood sugar levels which can prevent fat storage. These veggies are low in calories yet they're nutrient dense and will help you stay on track with your fat loss goals. When it comes to healthy fats, don't be afraid to add them to your diet. Avocado, olive oil, and nuts are packed with healthy fats that support fat metabolism and help you burn fat. These fats keep you feeling full and satisfied, making it easier to avoid overeating. Healthy fats also support your hormones which play a key role in fat breakdown. So don't shy away from these foods. They're essential for your fat burning journey and overall health. To give your metabolism an extra boost, green tea is a fantastic addition to your diet. This magical drink is rich in antioxidants called catechins which have been shown to increase fat oxidation and boost metabolism. Drinking green tea, especially when combined with exercise, can help you burn more fat. It's a simple, refreshing way to enhance your fat burning efforts and keep your metabolism active throughout the day. Another great food for fat loss is Greek yogurt. This creamy treat is packed with protein and probiotics which are beneficial for gut health. A healthy gut can improve digestion and even support fat loss. Greek yogurt is also a great source of calcium which has been linked to fat breakdown. So make it a habit to include Greek yogurt in your diet. It's a delicious and nutritious way to help your body burn fat. Don't forget about lean meats like turkey and fish. These foods are high in protein and low in unhealthy fats. Making them perfect for fat loss. They also provide essential nutrients like omega-3 fatty acids which can help increase your metabolism and promote fat burning. Foods rich in omega-3s such as salmon, chia seeds and walnuts not only support heart health but also boost your body's ability to burn fat more efficiently. Lastly, water is often overlooked but is essential for fat loss. Eating hydrated helps your metabolism function at its best. If you're not drinking enough water, your metabolism could slow down, making it harder for your body to burn fat. Plus, dehydration can sometimes be mistaken for hunger, causing you to eat more than you actually need. Drinking plenty of water throughout the day helps keep your metabolism running smoothly and can even reduce bloating, making you feel lighter and more energized. So, if you're serious about burning fat, start incorporating these fat burning foods into your diet. Focus on protein, fiber-rich vegetables, healthy fats and nutrient-packed options like green tea and Greek yogurt. These foods will help you feel full, boost your metabolism and support fat loss in a sustainable way. By making these smart food choices, you'll set yourself up for success on your fat burning journey. We're eating these foods today and watch your body transform.
